points.title: A あるいは B (A aruiwa B)
points.meaning: Indicates alternatives; 'A or B', 'either A or B'.
points.explanation: The あるいは grammar point is used to show alternatives or options, similar to 'A or B' or 'either A or B' in English. It highlights the possibility of more than one option in a situation. It can be used with verbs, adjectives, and nouns.
points.short: Indicates alternatives; 'A or B', 'either A or B'.
points.long: The あるいは grammar point is used to show alternatives or options, similar to 'A or B' or 'either A or B' in English. It highlights the possibility of more than one option in a situation. It can be used with verbs, adjectives, and nouns.
formation: Phrase A + あるいは + Phrase B

examples.jp: 今日は映画を見るあるいはショッピングをする予定です。
examples.ja: 今日は映画を見るあるいはショッピングをする予定です。
examples.romaji: Kyou wa eiga wo miru aruiwa shoppingu wo suru yotei desu.
examples.en: Today, I plan to watch a movie or go shopping.

cloze.after: ショッピングをする予定です。

examples.literalEn: Today, I plan to either watch a movie or go shopping.
examples.naturalEn: Today, I plan to watch a movie or go shopping.

examples.jp: 彼女は英語あるいはドイツ語で話すことができます。
examples.ja: 彼女は英語あるいはドイツ語で話すことができます。
examples.romaji: Kanojo wa eigo aruiwa doitsugo de hanasu koto ga dekimasu.
examples.en: She can speak English or German.

cloze.after: ドイツ語で話すことができます。

examples.literalEn: She can speak either English or German.
examples.naturalEn: She can speak English or German.

examples.jp: 僕らはコーヒーあるいは紅茶を飲むのが好きです。
examples.ja: 僕らはコーヒーあるいは紅茶を飲むのが好きです。
examples.romaji: Bokura wa koohii aruiwa koucha wo nomu no ga suki desu.
examples.en: We like to drink coffee or tea.

cloze.after: 紅茶を飲むのが好きです。

examples.literalEn: We like to drink either coffee or tea.
examples.naturalEn: We like to drink coffee or tea.

examples.jp: この仕事は正社員あるいは契約社員として働くことができます。
examples.ja: この仕事は正社員あるいは契約社員として働くことができます。
examples.romaji: Kono shigoto wa seishain aruiwa keiyaku shain toshite hataraku koto ga dekimasu.
examples.en: You can work in this position as a full-time employee or a contract employee.

cloze.after: 契約社員として働くことができます。

examples.literalEn: You can work as either a full-time employee or a contract employee in this job.
examples.naturalEn: You can work in this position as a full-time employee or a contract employee.

notes.nuance: This expression, “A or B,” means “Indicates alternatives; ‘A or B,’ ‘either A or B.’” It is an important grammar point at the JLPT N2 level and is widely used in objective explanations and everyday conversation.
notes.contrast: When compared to other particles and conjunctive forms used in context, “A or B” has the characteristic of clearly indicating the speaker’s intent and focus.
notes.pitfalls: Please be careful of conjugation errors in the "Phrase A + あるいは + Phrase B" structure. It is important to use the dictionary form and the "te" form correctly and to choose the appropriate particles.

points.title: A。おまけに B。(~omake ni)
points.meaning: Expresses that in addition to A, there is also B; 'moreover', 'besides', 'not only', 'but also'.
points.explanation: The A。おまけに B。grammar point is used to express that in addition to the first statement A, there is also the second statement B which often emphasizes the negative aspect or difficulty of the situation. It can be translated as 'moreover', 'besides', 'not only', or 'but also' in English. The formation is used with two sentences, placing おまけに between those two sentences.
points.short: Expresses that in addition to A, there is also B; 'moreover', 'besides', 'not only', 'but also'.
points.long: The A。おまけに B。grammar point is used to express that in addition to the first statement A, there is also the second statement B which often emphasizes the negative aspect or difficulty of the situation. It can be translated as 'moreover', 'besides', 'not only', or 'but also' in English. The formation is used with two sentences, placing おまけに between those two sentences.
formation: Sentence A + おまけに  + Sentence B

examples.jp: 彼は遅刻した。おまけに宿題も忘れた。
examples.ja: 彼は遅刻した。おまけに宿題も忘れた。
examples.romaji: Kare wa chikoku shita. Omake ni shukudai mo wasureta.
examples.en: He was late. On top of that, he forgot his homework.
examples.literalEn: He was late. Moreover, he forgot his homework.
examples.naturalEn: He was late. On top of that, he forgot his homework.

examples.jp: このアパートは狭い。おまけに家賃が高い。
examples.ja: このアパートは狭い。おまけに家賃が高い。
examples.romaji: Kono apaato wa semai. Omake ni yachin ga takai.
examples.en: This apartment is small. On top of that, the rent is high.
examples.literalEn: This apartment is small. Besides, the rent is high.
examples.naturalEn: This apartment is small. On top of that, the rent is high.

examples.jp: 彼女は仕事が忙しい。おまけに子供も小さい。
examples.ja: 彼女は仕事が忙しい。おまけに子供も小さい。
examples.romaji: Kanojo wa shigoto ga isogashii. Omake ni kodomo mo chiisai.
examples.en: She’s busy with work. On top of that, her children are still young.
examples.literalEn: She is busy with work. Not only that, her children are also small.
examples.naturalEn: She’s busy with work. On top of that, her children are still young.

examples.jp: 昨日は雨が降った。おまけに風も強かった。
examples.ja: 昨日は雨が降った。おまけに風も強かった。
examples.romaji: Kinou wa ame ga futta. Omake ni kaze mo tsuyokatta.
examples.en: It rained yesterday. On top of that, the wind was strong.
examples.literalEn: Yesterday it rained. In addition, the wind was strong.
examples.naturalEn: It rained yesterday. On top of that, the wind was strong.

notes.nuance: This expression, “A. Moreover, B,” means “Expresses that in addition to A, there is also B; ‘moreover,’ ‘besides,’ ‘not only,’ ‘but also.’” It is an important grammar point at the JLPT N2 level and is widely used in objective explanations and everyday conversation.
notes.contrast: When compared to other particles and conjunctive forms used in context, the phrase “A. Moreover, B.” clearly indicates the speaker’s intent and focus.
notes.pitfalls: Please be careful of errors in verb conjugation when using the "Sentence A + moreover + Sentence B" structure. It is important to use the dictionary form, the "te" form, and the correct particles accurately.

points.title: A。さて B。(A. Sate B.)
points.meaning: Indicates a sudden change or shift in the topic or situation; 'now then', 'well', 'so'.
points.explanation: The さて grammar point is used to indicate a sudden change or shift in the topic or situation. It often expresses a sense of moving on to the next topic or action, acting as a connector between sentences. It can be loosely translated as 'now then', 'well', or 'so' in English.
points.short: Indicates a sudden change or shift in the topic or situation; 'now then', 'well', 'so'.
points.long: The さて grammar point is used to indicate a sudden change or shift in the topic or situation. It often expresses a sense of moving on to the next topic or action, acting as a connector between sentences. It can be loosely translated as 'now then', 'well', or 'so' in English.
formation: A + さて + B

examples.jp: 今日の仕事が終わった。さて、これから帰るか。
examples.ja: 今日の仕事が終わった。さて、これから帰るか。
examples.romaji: Kyou no shigoto ga owatta. Sate, kore kara kaeru ka.
examples.en: I’m done with work for today. Well, I guess I’ll head home now.

cloze.before: 今日の仕事が終わった。

examples.literalEn: Today's work is done. Now then, shall we go home?
examples.naturalEn: I’m done with work for today. Well, I guess I’ll head home now.

examples.jp: 話がちょっと長くなったね。さて、もっと喜美子さんのことを教えてください。
examples.ja: 話がちょっと長くなったね。さて、もっと喜美子さんのことを教えてください。
examples.romaji: Hanashi ga chotto nagaku natta ne. Sate, motto Kimiko-san no koto wo oshiete kudasai.
examples.en: This has gone on a bit, hasn’t it? Now, please tell me more about Kimiko.

cloze.before: 話がちょっと長くなったね。
cloze.after: 、もっと喜美子さんのことを教えてください。

examples.literalEn: The conversation got a bit lengthy. Well, please tell me more about Kimiko.
examples.naturalEn: This has gone on a bit, hasn’t it? Now, please tell me more about Kimiko.

examples.jp: 映画を見て楽しかった。さて、何を食べに行こう。
examples.ja: 映画を見て楽しかった。さて、何を食べに行こう。
examples.romaji: Eiga wo mite tanoshikatta. Sate, nani wo tabe ni ikou.
examples.en: I had fun watching the movie. Now, where should we go to eat?

cloze.before: 映画を見て楽しかった。

examples.literalEn: Watching the movie was fun. So, what shall we go eat?
examples.naturalEn: I had fun watching the movie. Now, where should we go to eat?

examples.jp: マラソンが終わった！さて、少し休んでからシャワーを浴びよう。
examples.ja: マラソンが終わった！さて、少し休んでからシャワーを浴びよう。
examples.romaji: Marason ga owatta! Sate, sukoshi yasunde kara shawaa wo abiyou.
examples.en: The marathon is over! Now, I’ll take a short break and then take a shower.

cloze.after: 、少し休んでからシャワーを浴びよう。

examples.literalEn: The marathon is over! Now then, let's rest a bit and then take a shower.
examples.naturalEn: The marathon is over! Now, I’ll take a short break and then take a shower.

notes.nuance: This expression, “A. Now then, B,” indicates a sudden change or shift in the topic or situation; it translates to “now then,” “well,” or “so.” It is an important grammar point at the JLPT N2 level and is widely used in objective explanations and everyday conversation.
notes.contrast: When compared to other particles and conjunctive forms used in different contexts, the phrase “A. Now, B.” clearly indicates the speaker’s intent and focus.
notes.pitfalls: Please be careful not to make mistakes in conjugation when using the "A + さて + B" structure. It is important to use the dictionary form, the "te" form, and the correct particles accurately.

points.title: A。しかも B。(A. Shikamo B.)
points.meaning: Expressing additional information; 'moreover', 'besides', 'furthermore'.
points.explanation: The しかも grammar point is used to express additional information, supplementing or emphasizing what was mentioned before. It can be translated as 'moreover', 'besides', or 'furthermore' in English. Both A and B are independent statements, and しかも is used to connect them.
points.short: Expressing additional information; 'moreover', 'besides', 'furthermore'.
points.long: The しかも grammar point is used to express additional information, supplementing or emphasizing what was mentioned before. It can be translated as 'moreover', 'besides', or 'furthermore' in English. Both A and B are independent statements, and しかも is used to connect them.
formation: Statement A + 。しかも + Statement B。

examples.jp: この料理は美味しいです。しかも、安いです。
examples.ja: この料理は美味しいです。しかも、安いです。
examples.romaji: Kono ryouri wa oishii desu. Shikamo, yasui desu.
examples.en: This dish is delicious. Plus, it’s inexpensive.

cloze.before: この料理は美味しいです。

examples.literalEn: This dish is delicious. Moreover, it is cheap.
examples.naturalEn: This dish is delicious. Plus, it’s inexpensive.

examples.jp: 彼は優秀な学生です。しかも、スポーツが得意です。
examples.ja: 彼は優秀な学生です。しかも、スポーツが得意です。
examples.romaji: Kare wa yuushuu na gakusei desu. Shikamo, supootsu ga tokui desu.
examples.en: He is an excellent student. What’s more, he’s good at sports.
examples.literalEn: He is an excellent student. Besides, he is good at sports.
examples.naturalEn: He is an excellent student. What’s more, he’s good at sports.

examples.jp: 彼女は歌が上手です。しかも、ダンスも上手です。
examples.ja: 彼女は歌が上手です。しかも、ダンスも上手です。
examples.romaji: Kanojo wa uta ga jouzu desu. Shikamo, dansu mo jouzu desu.
examples.en: She sings well. What’s more, she’s a good dancer, too.
examples.literalEn: She is good at singing. Furthermore, she is also good at dancing.
examples.naturalEn: She sings well. What’s more, she’s a good dancer, too.

examples.jp: このカフェは雰囲気がいいです。しかも、コーヒーも美味しいです。
examples.ja: このカフェは雰囲気がいいです。しかも、コーヒーも美味しいです。
examples.romaji: Kono kafe wa fun'iki ga ii desu. Shikamo, koohii mo oishii desu.
examples.en: This café has a nice atmosphere. Plus, the coffee is delicious.

cloze.before: このカフェは雰囲気がいいです。

examples.literalEn: This cafe has a nice atmosphere. Moreover, the coffee is also delicious.
examples.naturalEn: This café has a nice atmosphere. Plus, the coffee is delicious.

notes.nuance: This expression, “A. Moreover, B.,” is used to “Express additional information; ‘moreover,’ ‘besides,’ ‘furthermore.’” It is an important grammar point at the JLPT N2 level and is widely used in objective explanations and everyday conversation.
notes.contrast: When compared to other particles and conjunctive forms used in different contexts, the phrase “A. Moreover, B.” clearly indicates the speaker’s intent and focus.
notes.pitfalls: Please be careful of verb conjugation errors in this type of construction (Statement A + “Moreover” + Statement B). It is important to use the dictionary form and the “te” form correctly and to choose the appropriate particles.

points.title: A。したがって B。(A. Shitagatte B.)
points.meaning: Express a cause-and-effect relationship; 'therefore', 'consequently', 'so'.
points.explanation: The したがって grammar point is used to express a cause-and-effect relationship between two sentences, where 'A' is the cause and 'B' is the effect, result or conclusion. It can be translated as 'therefore', 'consequently', or 'so' in English.
points.short: Express a cause-and-effect relationship; 'therefore', 'consequently', 'so'.
points.long: The したがって grammar point is used to express a cause-and-effect relationship between two sentences, where 'A' is the cause and 'B' is the effect, result or conclusion. It can be translated as 'therefore', 'consequently', or 'so' in English.
formation: A + したがって + B

examples.jp: 今日は雨が降っています。したがって、傘を持って行きましょう。
examples.ja: 今日は雨が降っています。したがって、傘を持って行きましょう。
examples.romaji: Kyou wa ame ga futteimasu. Shitagatte, kasa wo motte ikimashou.
examples.en: It’s raining today. Therefore, let’s take an umbrella with us.

cloze.before: 今日は雨が降っています。

examples.literalEn: It is raining today. Therefore, let's bring an umbrella.
examples.naturalEn: It’s raining today. Therefore, let’s take an umbrella with us.

examples.jp: 彼は忙しいです。したがって、彼に連絡するのはやめましょう。
examples.ja: 彼は忙しいです。したがって、彼に連絡するのはやめましょう。
examples.romaji: Kare wa isogashii desu. Shitagatte, kare ni renraku suru no wa yamemashou.
examples.en: He is busy. Therefore, let’s not contact him.

cloze.after: 、彼に連絡するのはやめましょう。

examples.literalEn: He is busy. Consequently, let's not contact him.
examples.naturalEn: He is busy. Therefore, let’s not contact him.

examples.jp: そのレストランは人気があります。したがって、予約しないと席がないかもしれません。
examples.ja: そのレストランは人気があります。したがって、予約しないと席がないかもしれません。
examples.romaji: Sono resutoran wa ninki ga arimasu. Shitagatte, yoyaku shinai to seki ga nai kamoshiremasen.
examples.en: That restaurant is popular. Therefore, you might not be able to get a seat without a reservation.

cloze.before: そのレストランは人気があります。
cloze.after: 、予約しないと席がないかもしれません。

examples.literalEn: That restaurant is popular. Therefore, there might be no seats if you don't make a reservation.
examples.naturalEn: That restaurant is popular. Therefore, you might not be able to get a seat without a reservation.

examples.jp: 試験が近いです。したがって、勉強に集中しましょう。
examples.ja: 試験が近いです。したがって、勉強に集中しましょう。
examples.romaji: Shiken ga chikai desu. Shitagatte, benkyou ni shuuchuu shimashou.
examples.en: The exam is coming up soon. Therefore, let’s focus on studying.
examples.literalEn: The exam is coming up soon. Consequently, let's focus on studying.
examples.naturalEn: The exam is coming up soon. Therefore, let’s focus on studying.

notes.nuance: This expression, “A. Therefore, B.,” is used to “express a cause-and-effect relationship; ‘therefore,’ ‘consequently,’ ‘so.’” It is an important grammar point at the JLPT N2 level and is widely used in objective explanations and everyday conversation.
notes.contrast: Compared to other particles and conjunctive forms used in different contexts, the structure “A. Therefore, B.” clearly indicates the speaker’s intent and focus.
notes.pitfalls: Please be careful of mistakes in conjugation when using the "A + therefore + B" structure. It is important to use the dictionary form, the "te" form, and the correct particles accurately.

points.title: A すなわち B。 (A sunawachi B)
points.meaning: Express that A is equivalent to B; 'in other words', 'namely', 'that is to say'.
points.explanation: The grammar point A すなわち B is used to express that two phrases are equivalent or that the second phrase is further explanation, clarification or the true meaning of the first phrase. This can be translated as 'in other words', 'namely', or 'that is to say' in English.
points.short: Express that A is equivalent to B; 'in other words', 'namely', 'that is to say'.
points.long: The grammar point A すなわち B is used to express that two phrases are equivalent or that the second phrase is further explanation, clarification or the true meaning of the first phrase. This can be translated as 'in other words', 'namely', or 'that is to say' in English.
formation: Phrase A + すなわち + Phrase B

examples.jp: 私は立派な成果を出したい、すなわち、成功したいのです。
examples.ja: 私は立派な成果を出したい、すなわち、成功したいのです。
examples.romaji: Watashi wa rippana seika wo dashitai, sunawachi, seikou shitai no desu.
examples.en: I want to achieve great results—in other words, I want to succeed.

cloze.before: 私は立派な成果を出したい、

examples.literalEn: I want to achieve great results, in other words, I want to succeed.
examples.naturalEn: I want to achieve great results—in other words, I want to succeed.

examples.jp: 彼は言葉に詰まった、すなわち、何も言えなかった。
examples.ja: 彼は言葉に詰まった、すなわち、何も言えなかった。
examples.romaji: Kare wa kotoba ni tsumatta, sunawachi, nani mo ienakatta.
examples.en: He was at a loss for words—in other words, he couldn’t say anything.
examples.literalEn: He was at a loss for words, that is to say, he couldn't say anything.
examples.naturalEn: He was at a loss for words—in other words, he couldn’t say anything.

examples.jp: 彼女は自分の目標に向かって努力し続けている、すなわち、彼女は非常に頑張っている。
examples.ja: 彼女は自分の目標に向かって努力し続けている、すなわち、彼女は非常に頑張っている。
examples.romaji: Kanojo wa jibun no mokuhyou ni mukatte doryoku shi tsudzukete iru, sunawachi, kanojo wa hijou ni ganbatte iru.
examples.en: She continues to work hard toward her goals; in other words, she is working very hard.

cloze.before: 彼女は自分の目標に向かって努力し続けている、
cloze.after: 、彼女は非常に頑張っている。

examples.literalEn: She keeps working hard towards her goals, namely, she is trying very hard.
examples.naturalEn: She continues to work hard toward her goals; in other words, she is working very hard.

examples.jp: この店はお客様の満足を一番大事にしています、すなわち、サービスが良いということです。
examples.ja: この店はお客様の満足を一番大事にしています、すなわち、サービスが良いということです。
examples.romaji: Kono mise wa okyakusama no manzoku o ichiban daiji ni shiteimasu, sunawachi, saabisu ga yoi to iu koto desu.
examples.en: This store places the highest priority on customer satisfaction—in other words, it provides excellent service.

cloze.before: この店はお客様の満足を一番大事にしています、
cloze.after: 、サービスが良いということです。

examples.literalEn: This store values customer satisfaction above all else, in other words, it has good service.
examples.naturalEn: This store places the highest priority on customer satisfaction—in other words, it provides excellent service.

notes.nuance: The expression “A, namely B” means “Express that A is equivalent to B; ‘in other words,’ ‘namely,’ ‘that is to say.’” It is an important grammar point at the JLPT N2 level and is widely used in objective explanations and everyday conversation.
notes.contrast: When compared to other particles and conjunctive forms used in context, “A, namely B” is characterized by its ability to clearly indicate the speaker’s intent and focus.
notes.pitfalls: Please be careful of mistakes in conjugation when using the "namely" construction (Phrase A + namely + Phrase B). It is important to use the dictionary form, the "te" form, and the correct particles accurately.

points.title: A。すると B。(~suruto)
points.meaning: Indicates that when action A is done, action or event B follows; 'then', 'when', 'if'.
points.explanation: The A。すると B。grammar point is used to express that when action A is done or takes place, action or event B follows. It can be translated as 'then', 'when', or 'if' in English. It is used to show a natural consequence or result of action A.
points.short: Indicates that when action A is done, action or event B follows; 'then', 'when', 'if'.
points.long: The A。すると B。grammar point is used to express that when action A is done or takes place, action or event B follows. It can be translated as 'then', 'when', or 'if' in English. It is used to show a natural consequence or result of action A.
formation: A (Sentence) + すると + B (Sentence)

examples.jp: 電話をかけると、彼女が出ました。

examples.naturalEn: As soon as he left the house, it started to rain.

examples.naturalEn: Once he confirmed she was safe, his anxiety subsided.

examples.jp: 運動をするとすぐに汗をかく。

examples.naturalEn: I start sweating as soon as I exercise.

examples.jp: みんなの前で発表するときは、まっすぐ前を向くように気をつけてください。

points.title: A。そういえば B。(~souieba)
points.meaning: Recalling something related to A; 'speaking of which', 'by the way', 'now that you mention it'.
points.explanation: The A。そういえば B。grammar point is used when something related to A is recalled or brought up. It is commonly used to connect two related topics or ideas in a conversation and indicates a change of focus. The formation consists of two clauses: the first being A and the second being B, with 'そういえば' in between as a connector.

points.title: A。それがB。(~sorega)
points.meaning: Expressing 'that's exactly what A is; in other words, B'.
points.explanation: The grammar point A。それがB。can be used to restate or clarify that B is precisely what A means. It emphasizes the essence or definition of A by stating B. It can be translated as 'that’s what A is,' 'that is precisely A/B,' or 'in other words, B.'
points.short: Expressing 'that's exactly what A is; in other words, B'.
points.long: The grammar point A。それがB。can be used to restate or clarify that B is precisely what A means. It emphasizes the essence or definition of A by stating B. It can be translated as 'that’s what A is,' 'that is precisely A/B,' or 'in other words, B.'

notes.nuance: This expression, “A. By the way, B,” means “Used to give additional information about the topic; ‘by the way,’ ‘incidentally.’” It is an important grammar point at the JLPT N2 level and is widely used in objective explanations and everyday conversation.

points.title: A。ということは B。 (A. To iu koto wa B.)
points.meaning: Expresses the meaning 'if A, that means B' or 'A implies B'.
points.explanation: The A。ということは B。grammar point is used to express the logical conclusion that if A is true, then B must also be true. It can be translated as 'if A, that means B' or 'A implies B' in English. This pattern is used when the speaker wants to infer or deduce B based on the information provided by A.
points.romaji: A. To iu koto wa B.
points.short: Expresses the meaning 'if A, that means B' or 'A implies B'.
points.long: The A。ということは B。grammar point is used to express the logical conclusion that if A is true, then B must also be true. It can be translated as 'if A, that means B' or 'A implies B' in English. This pattern is used when the speaker wants to infer or deduce B based on the information provided by A.
formation: A + ということは + B

points.title: A。というのは B。(Toiu no wa~)
points.meaning: Used to give an explanation or provide additional information for A; 'that is to say', 'in other words'.
points.explanation: The grammar point A。というのは B。 is used to provide an explanation, definition, or further information about statement A. It can be translated as 'that is to say', 'in other words', or 'namely' in English.
points.short: Used to give an explanation or provide additional information for A; 'that is to say', 'in other words'.
points.long: The grammar point A。というのは B。 is used to provide an explanation, definition, or further information about statement A. It can be translated as 'that is to say', 'in other words', or 'namely' in English.
formation: [Statement A]。というのは、[Statement B]。

points.title: A。なおB。(A. Nao B.)
points.meaning: Provides additional information; 'moreover', 'besides', 'in addition'.
points.explanation: The なお grammar point is used to provide additional information or emphasize an existing fact. It can be translated as 'moreover', 'besides', or 'in addition' in English. なお is placed between two sentences to connect them and provide supplementary information.
points.short: Provides additional information; 'moreover', 'besides', 'in addition'.
points.long: The なお grammar point is used to provide additional information or emphasize an existing fact. It can be translated as 'moreover', 'besides', or 'in addition' in English. なお is placed between two sentences to connect them and provide supplementary information.
formation: A (sentence) + なお + B (sentence)

points.title: A。もっとも B。(Motto mo ~)

points.explanation: The A。もっとも B。 grammar point is used to express contrasting opinions or facts. It can be translated as 'although', 'but', or 'however' in English. This structure connects two clauses and highlights the contrast between them.
points.short: Express contrasting opinions or facts; 'although', 'but', 'however'.
points.long: The A。もっとも B。 grammar point is used to express contrasting opinions or facts. It can be translated as 'although', 'but', or 'however' in English. This structure connects two clauses and highlights the contrast between them.
formation: Clause A + もっとも + Clause B

points.title: A。要するに B。(A. Yousuru ni B.)
points.meaning: Expressing 'in short', 'in a nutshell', or 'to sum up' when restating or summarizing A as B.
points.explanation: The A。要するに B。grammar point is used to restate or summarize the information provided in A more concisely as B. It can be translated as 'in short', 'in a nutshell', or 'to sum up' in English. The formation consists of two sentences or statements, A and B, with 要するに (yousuru ni) in between to indicate the summary or restatement of A as B.
points.short: Expressing 'in short', 'in a nutshell', or 'to sum up' when restating or summarizing A as B.
points.long: The A。要するに B。grammar point is used to restate or summarize the information provided in A more concisely as B. It can be translated as 'in short', 'in a nutshell', or 'to sum up' in English. The formation consists of two sentences or statements, A and B, with 要するに (yousuru ni) in between to indicate the summary or restatement of A as B.

points.title: Noun にて (Noun nite)
points.meaning: Expresses location or means; 'at', 'in', 'by', 'with'.

It functions similarly to the particle で, but にて is more formal and often used in written language, formal speaking, and announcements.
points.short: Expresses location or means; 'at', 'in', 'by', 'with'.

points.title: Noun を はじめ (Noun wo hajime)
points.meaning: Meaning 'starting with', 'including', 'not only... but also'.
points.explanation: The grammar point Nounをはじめ is used to show that there are other things or people being included apart from the mentioned noun. It can be used to provide an example, indicate a representative or list items. This can be translated as 'starting with', 'including', or 'not only... but also...' in English.
points.short: Meaning 'starting with', 'including', 'not only... but also'.
points.long: The grammar point Nounをはじめ is used to show that there are other things or people being included apart from the mentioned noun. It can be used to provide an example, indicate a representative or list items. This can be translated as 'starting with', 'including', or 'not only... but also...' in English.

points.title: Noun を はじめとして (Noun wo hajime to shite)
points.meaning: Expresses 'starting with', 'beginning with', or 'including'.
points.explanation: The grammar point Noun を はじめとして is used to emphasize a particular item or example along with others. It translates to 'starting with', 'beginning with', or 'including' in English. It is used to present a specific case and imply there are more related items.
points.pattern: Noun を はじめとして
points.short: Expresses 'starting with', 'beginning with', or 'including'.
points.long: The grammar point Noun を はじめとして is used to emphasize a particular item or example along with others. It translates to 'starting with', 'beginning with', or 'including' in English. It is used to present a specific case and imply there are more related items.

points.title: Noun を めぐって (Noun wo megutte)
points.meaning: Concerning; with regard to; about
points.explanation: The grammar point Noun を めぐって is used to express that something is concerning, with regard to or about a certain noun. It covers a topic or an issue that is central to a discussion or a situation.
points.short: Concerning; with regard to; about
points.long: The grammar point Noun を めぐって is used to express that something is concerning, with regard to or about a certain noun. It covers a topic or an issue that is central to a discussion or a situation.

points.title: Noun を めぐる Noun (Noun o meguru Noun)
points.meaning: Indicate a situation or event revolving around a particular noun; 'concerning', 'regarding', 'pertaining to'.
points.explanation: The NounをめぐるNoun grammar point is used to express that a situation or event is centered around a particular noun. It can be translated as 'concerning', 'regarding', or 'pertaining to' in English. The formation consists of the particle 'を' placed between two nouns, and the verb 'めぐる' (to revolve around) following the first noun.
points.pattern: Noun を めぐる Noun

points.explanation: The 'Noun をもとにして' grammar point is used to express that something is done based on, using, or utilizing the noun. It indicates that the noun is the foundation, source or basis for the action or statement.

points.title: Verb ことなく (~kotonaku)
points.meaning: Means 'without doing', 'not doing', or 'without happening'.
points.explanation: The grammar point ことなく is added to the stem of a verb to express that something doesn't happen or isn't done. It can be translated as 'without doing', 'not doing', or 'without happening'. The formation depends on whether it is used with a verb.

points.title: Verb ないことには Verb ない (~nai koto ni wa ~ nai)
points.meaning: Express that something cannot be done without meeting a certain condition.
points.explanation: The ないことには grammar point is used to indicate that something cannot be done or achieved unless a certain condition is met. This pattern is formed by attaching ないことには to the negative form of a verb, followed by a negative outcome statement. It often appears as V-ない + ことには + V-ない or a negative expression.
points.pattern: Verb ないことには Verb ない
points.short: Express that something cannot be done without meeting a certain condition.
points.long: The ないことには grammar point is used to indicate that something cannot be done or achieved unless a certain condition is met. points.title: ～あげく (~ageku)
points.meaning: Expresses the outcome of a series of actions or events; 'in the end', 'finally', 'after'.
points.explanation: The ～あげく grammar point is used to express the outcome or result after a series of actions or events. It can usually be translated into English as 'in the end', 'finally', or 'after'. The typical formation is adding あげく to the past form of a verb (Verb-た), or adding のあげく to a noun. This indicates that, after a long process or a number of attempts, a certain final outcome is reached—often with a sense that it took considerable effort or time.
points.short: Expresses the outcome of a series of actions or events; 'in the end', 'finally', 'after'.
points.long: The ～あげく grammar point is used to express the outcome or result after a series of actions or events. It can usually be translated into English as 'in the end', 'finally', or 'after'. The typical formation is adding あげく to the past form of a verb (Verb-た), or adding のあげく to a noun. This indicates that, after a long process or a number of attempts, a certain final outcome is reached—often with a sense that it took considerable effort or time.

points.title: ～うちに (〜uchi ni)
points.meaning: Expresses doing something while a certain condition still holds; 'while', 'before', 'as long as'.

points.title: ～かねる (〜kaneru)
points.meaning: Express inability or impossibility of doing an action (often as a polite refusal).
points.explanation: The ～かねる grammar point is used to express that someone cannot do an action or that something is impossible to do. It typically has a nuance of reluctance or polite refusal and is formed by adding かねる to the ます-stem of the verb.
points.short: Express inability or impossibility of doing an action (often as a polite refusal).

points.title: ～かのようだ (〜ka no you da)
points.meaning: Express a similarity or comparison; 'as if', 'like', 'as though'.
points.explanation: The ～かのようだ grammar point is used to express similarity or comparison between two things or situations. It can be translated as 'as if', 'like', or 'as though' in English. points.title: ～か～まいか (〜ka 〜maika)

points.explanation: The ～か～まいか grammar point expresses uncertainty or indecision, often with a more formal or literary feel. points.title: ～から～にかけて (〜kara 〜ni kakete)
points.meaning: Expresses a range of time, space, or quantities; 'from...to', 'between...and', 'over'.
points.explanation: The ～から～にかけて grammar pattern is used to indicate a range or scope—often in time or space. It can be translated as 'from...to', 'between...and', or 'over' in English.

points.title: ～からには (〜kara niwa)
points.meaning: Express a sense of responsibility or determination; 'since', 'now that', 'if'.
points.explanation: The ～からには grammar point is used to show a sense of responsibility or strong resolve once a certain condition is met. It can be translated as 'since', 'now that', or 'if'.
points.short: Express a sense of responsibility or determination; 'since', 'now that', 'if'.
points.long: The ～からには grammar point is used to show a sense of responsibility or strong resolve once a certain condition is met. It can be translated as 'since', 'now that', or 'if'.

points.title: ～から見ると (〜kara miru to)
points.meaning: Express a perspective or point of view; 'from the standpoint of', 'in terms of', 'from the perspective of'.
points.explanation: The ～から見ると grammar point is used to express a particular perspective or point of view. In English, it translates to 'from the standpoint of', 'from the perspective of', or 'in terms of'. It is usually used with a noun that indicates the perspective.
points.short: Express a perspective or point of view; 'from the standpoint of', 'in terms of', 'from the perspective of'.
points.long: The ～から見ると grammar point is used to express a particular perspective or point of view. In English, it translates to 'from the standpoint of', 'from the perspective of', or 'in terms of'. It is usually used with a noun that indicates the perspective.

points.title: ～から言うと (〜kara iuto)
points.meaning: Express a judgment or opinion based on a specific criterion; 'speaking from', 'in terms of', 'from the viewpoint of'.
points.explanation: The ～から言うと grammar point is used to express a judgment or opinion based on a specific criterion or aspect. It can be translated as 'speaking from', 'in terms of', or 'from the viewpoint of' in English. It is most commonly used with nouns, although you may occasionally see other forms (like adjectives).
points.short: Express a judgment or opinion based on a specific criterion; 'speaking from', 'in terms of', 'from the viewpoint of'.

points.title: ～くせに (〜kuse ni)
points.meaning: Used to criticize someone for doing something contrary to what one would expect from their nature or situation.
points.explanation: The grammar point ～くせに is used to express criticism or disapproval toward someone who does something contradictory to their expected nature, role, or prior statement. It's used in fairly casual or spoken contexts and can sound quite critical or accusing. Note that there's a colloquial variant ～くせして, but ～くせに is the standard form taught in most references.
points.short: Used to criticize someone for doing something contrary to what one would expect from their nature or situation.
points.long: The grammar point ～くせに is used to express criticism or disapproval toward someone who does something contradictory to their expected nature, role, or prior statement. points.title: ～ことから (〜koto kara)

points.short: Indicates the reason or basis for something; 'because', 'since', 'due to'.

points.title: ～ことになっている (〜koto ni natte iru)
points.meaning: Expresses that something is supposed to be or has been decided (rule, plan, custom).
points.explanation: The ～ことになっている grammar point is used when something has been decided, planned, or there is a rule/custom that everyone follows. It can be translated as 'it is supposed to be,' 'it is decided,' or 'it is customary that.'
points.short: Expresses that something is supposed to be or has been decided (rule, plan, custom).
points.long: The ～ことになっている grammar point is used when something has been decided, planned, or there is a rule/custom that everyone follows. It can be translated as 'it is supposed to be,' 'it is decided,' or 'it is customary that.'

points.title: ～さえ～ば (〜sae ~ba)
points.meaning: Expresses that, as long as a certain condition is met, something else will follow; 'if only', 'provided that'.
points.explanation: The ～さえ～ば grammar point is used to indicate that if a certain single condition is fulfilled, everything else will be fine or a certain result will occur. It often translates as 'as long as...' or 'if only...'.
points.short: Expresses that, as long as a certain condition is met, something else will follow; 'if only', 'provided that'.
points.long: The ～さえ～ば grammar point is used to indicate that if a certain single condition is fulfilled, everything else will be fine or a certain result will occur. It often translates as 'as long as...' or 'if only...'.

points.title: ～ざるを得ない (〜zaru wo enai)
points.meaning: Have no choice but to; cannot help but.
points.explanation: The ～ざるを得ない grammar point is used to indicate that one has no choice but to do something or cannot avoid doing it. It is formed from the negative form (ない) but replaces ない with ざる, followed by を得ない. (Note: する → せざるを得ない.)
points.short: Have no choice but to; cannot help but.
points.long: The ～ざるを得ない grammar point is used to indicate that one has no choice but to do something or cannot avoid doing it. It is formed from the negative form (ない) but replaces ない with ざる, followed by を得ない. (Note: する → せざるを得ない.)

examples.jp: この仕事は締め切りが近いので、残業せざるを得ない。

examples.romaji: Kono shigoto wa shimekiri ga chikai no de, zangyou sezaru wo enai.

points.title: ～ずにはいられない (〜zu ni wa irarenai)
points.meaning: Cannot help but; cannot resist doing; an irresistible urge.
points.explanation: The ～ずにはいられない grammar point expresses that one cannot resist or help doing something. In other words, there is a strong urge that one cannot suppress. It's formed from the negative stem of a verb plus ずにはいられない. (Note: する → せずにはいられない.)
points.short: Cannot help but; cannot resist doing; an irresistible urge.
points.long: The ～ずにはいられない grammar point expresses that one cannot resist or help doing something. In other words, there is a strong urge that one cannot suppress. It's formed from the negative stem of a verb plus ずにはいられない. (Note: する → せずにはいられない.)

points.title: ～そうにない (〜sou ni nai)

points.explanation: The ～そうにない grammar point is used to indicate that something does not appear likely to happen. Often translated as 'doesn't seem like' or 'not likely to...'. Attach そうにない to the verb stem or adjective stem.
points.short: Express the unlikelihood of something happening; 'not likely', 'doesn't seem'.

points.explanation: The ～たかと思ったら grammar point indicates that one action occurs almost immediately after another, often conveying surprise at how quickly it happens. It is frequently translated as 'as soon as...' or 'no sooner than...'.
points.short: Express a sequence of events happening in quick succession; 'as soon as', 'no sooner than'.
points.long: The ～たかと思ったら grammar point indicates that one action occurs almost immediately after another, often conveying surprise at how quickly it happens. It is frequently translated as 'as soon as...' or 'no sooner than...'.

points.title: ～たきり (〜takiri)
points.meaning: Express 'since then' or 'after'; used to indicate that an action occurred once and has not been repeated or that a state has continued since a certain event or time.
points.explanation: The ～たきり grammar point is used to express that an action occurred once and has not been repeated, or that a situation or state has continued since a certain event or time. It can be translated as 'since then', 'after', or 'one time only' in English.
points.short: Express 'since then' or 'after'; used to indicate that an action occurred once and has not been repeated or that a state has continued since a certain event or time.
points.long: The ～たきり grammar point is used to express that an action occurred once and has not been repeated, or that a situation or state has continued since a certain event or time. It can be translated as 'since then', 'after', or 'one time only' in English.

points.title: ～だけあって (〜dake atte)
points.meaning: Expresses that something is as expected or deserves its reputation.
points.explanation: The ～だけあって grammar point is used to indicate that something is as expected or deserves its reputation, based on certain facts or qualities. It can be translated as 'no wonder', 'as expected', or 'it is natural that' in English.
points.short: Expresses that something is as expected or deserves its reputation.

points.title: ～だけましだ (〜dake mashi da)
points.meaning: Expresses that although the situation isn’t ideal, it could be worse; 'it’s not great, but at least...'.
points.explanation: The ～だけましだ grammar point is used to compare two undesirable or less-than-ideal situations, saying that one is not good, but still better than the worse alternative. It often translates as 'at least (it’s only...)' or 'it could be worse.'
points.short: Expresses that although the situation isn’t ideal, it could be worse; 'it’s not great, but at least...'.
points.long: The ～だけましだ grammar point is used to compare two undesirable or less-than-ideal situations, saying that one is not good, but still better than the worse alternative. It often translates as 'at least (it’s only...)' or 'it could be worse.'

It is important to use the dictionary form and "te" form correctly and to choose the appropriate particles.

points.title: ～たところ (〜ta tokoro)
points.meaning: Used to describe an action that has just been completed, often followed by a result or observation.
points.explanation: The ～たところ grammar point is used when an action has just been completed and the speaker wants to describe an observation or result that follows. It can be translated as 'just finished doing something' or 'as soon as (I did something)...'.
points.short: Used to describe an action that has just been completed, often followed by a result or observation.
points.long: The ～たところ grammar point is used when an action has just been completed and the speaker wants to describe an observation or result that follows. It can be translated as 'just finished doing something' or 'as soon as (I did something)...'.
formation: Verb-past + ところ

points.title: ～たとたん (〜ta totan)
points.meaning: Express the moment something happens; 'as soon as', 'just when'.
points.explanation: The ～たとたん grammar point is used to express that an action or event occurred at the same moment another action or event happened. It can be translated as 'as soon as' or 'just when.' It requires the past tense of a verb.
points.short: Express the moment something happens; 'as soon as', 'just when'.
points.long: The ～たとたん grammar point is used to express that an action or event occurred at the same moment another action or event happened. It can be translated as 'as soon as' or 'just when.' It requires the past tense of a verb.

points.title: ～だらけ (〜darake)
points.meaning: Indicates that something is full of or covered with a certain (usually negative) characteristic.
points.explanation: The ～だらけ grammar point is used to express that something is full of, covered with, or filled with a certain characteristic. It frequently has a negative or undesirable nuance.
points.short: Indicates that something is full of or covered with a certain (usually negative) characteristic.
points.long: The ～だらけ grammar point is used to express that something is full of, covered with, or filled with a certain characteristic. It frequently has a negative or undesirable nuance.

points.title: ～っこない (〜kkonai)
points.meaning: Expresses the impossibility or very low probability of something happening; 'no way', 'impossible'.
points.explanation: The ～っこない grammar point is used to express that something is impossible or extremely unlikely. It’s formed by attaching ～っこない to the negative stem of a verb. It can be translated as 'no way', 'no chance', or 'impossible.'
points.short: Expresses the impossibility or very low probability of something happening; 'no way', 'impossible'.
points.long: The ～っこない grammar point is used to express that something is impossible or extremely unlikely. It’s formed by attaching ～っこない to the negative stem of a verb. It can be translated as 'no way', 'no chance', or 'impossible.'

points.title: ～つつ (〜tsutsu)
points.meaning: Shows two actions happening simultaneously or a contrast; 'while', 'although'.
points.explanation: The ～つつ grammar point is used to express two actions occurring simultaneously, or to show a contrast between an ongoing action and another factor. It can be translated as 'while' or 'although.' It is attached to a verb in its stem form.
points.short: Shows two actions happening simultaneously or a contrast; 'while', 'although'.
points.long: The ～つつ grammar point is used to express two actions occurring simultaneously, or to show a contrast between an ongoing action and another factor. It can be translated as 'while' or 'although.' It is attached to a verb in its stem form.

points.title: ～つつある (〜tsutsu aru)

points.explanation: The ～つつある grammar point is used to describe something that is in the middle of a gradual change or development. It can be translated as '(something) is in the process of ~ing.' The most common usage is with the verb stem plus つつある.
points.short: Expresses an ongoing process or gradual change.

points.title: ～っぱなし (〜ppanashi)

points.explanation: The ～っぱなし grammar point is used to express that something is left in a certain condition for an extended time or that an action continues without stopping. It attaches to the ます-stem of verbs.
points.short: Express a continuous action or state; 'left as is', 'non-stop'.
points.long: The ～っぱなし grammar point is used to express that something is left in a certain condition for an extended time or that an action continues without stopping. It attaches to the ます-stem of verbs.

points.title: ～っぽい (〜ppoi)
points.meaning: Indicates that something has the appearance, characteristics, or behavior of something else.
points.explanation: The ～っぽい grammar point is used when something or someone appears to have characteristics, traits, or a vibe that resemble something else. It can mean 'looks like,' 'seems like,' or 'has the quality of.'

points.title: ～ていられない (〜te irarenai)
points.meaning: Expresses that one cannot afford to do something; 'can't keep on', 'unable to continue'.
points.explanation: The ～ていられない grammar point is used to express a feeling of not being able to continue doing something or remaining in a certain state. It can be translated as 'can't keep on', 'unable to continue', or 'can't afford to' in English. The formation is the same for all verb types.
points.short: Expresses that one cannot afford to do something; 'can't keep on', 'unable to continue'.

points.title: ～てかなわない (〜te kanawanai)
points.meaning: Expresses that something cannot be endured, tolerated, or is unbearable.
points.explanation: The ～てかなわない grammar point is typically used with adjectives (or a rephrased verb) in 〜て form to show an unbearable situation or feeling. It means you 'can’t stand' or 'can’t endure' something. It often appears with expressions like 「暑くてかなわない」「うるさくてかなわない」 and so on.
points.short: Expresses that something cannot be endured, tolerated, or is unbearable.
points.long: The ～てかなわない grammar point is typically used with adjectives (or a rephrased verb) in 〜て form to show an unbearable situation or feeling. It means you 'can’t stand' or 'can’t endure' something. It often appears with expressions like 「暑くてかなわない」「うるさくてかなわない」 and so on.

points.title: ～てからでないと (〜te kara denai to)
points.meaning: Indicates that something cannot be done before a certain action is completed; 'not until', 'only after'.
points.explanation: The ～てからでないと grammar point is used to express that an action cannot be done before another action has been completed. It can be translated as 'not until' or 'only after' in English. It attaches to a verb in the て-form, plus からでないと.
points.short: Indicates that something cannot be done before a certain action is completed; 'not until', 'only after'.

points.explanation: The ～てこそ grammar point is used to emphasize that 'only when' or 'precisely because' the stated condition is met, a certain result or meaning arises. For nouns and adjectives, similar forms appear (e.g., Noun + でこそ, い-Adjective くてこそ, な-Adjective でこそ).
points.short: Emphasizes the condition; 'only when', 'precisely because'.

points.title: ～でしょうがない (〜deshou ga nai)

points.title: ～でならない (〜de naranai)
points.meaning: Indicates an uncontrollable emotion or feeling; 'can’t help but', 'overwhelmingly'.
points.explanation: The ～でならない grammar pattern expresses a very strong, often involuntary feeling—e.g., '不思議でならない' (it’s so mysterious I can’t help thinking about it), '残念でならない' (I’m so disappointed), '心配でならない' (I’m extremely worried).
points.short: Indicates an uncontrollable emotion or feeling; 'can’t help but', 'overwhelmingly'.
points.long: The ～でならない grammar pattern expresses a very strong, often involuntary feeling—e.g., '不思議でならない' (it’s so mysterious I can’t help thinking about it), '残念でならない' (I’m so disappointed), '心配でならない' (I’m extremely worried).

points.explanation: The ～でばかりはいられない grammar point is used when one realizes they cannot keep doing only that one thing or cannot always rely on a certain situation. It implies the need to take other actions or responsibilities.

points.long: The ～でばかりはいられない grammar point is used when one realizes they cannot keep doing only that one thing or cannot always rely on a certain situation. It implies the need to take other actions or responsibilities.

points.title: ～ではないか (〜de wa nai ka)
points.meaning: Used to show a strong assertion or emphasis on one’s opinion; 'isn't it?', 'aren't you?', 'right?'.
points.explanation: The ～ではないか grammar point is used at the end of a sentence to make a rhetorical question or a strong, emphatic statement. It often translates as 'isn't it…?' 'aren't you…?' or 'wouldn’t you say…?'.
points.short: Used to show a strong assertion or emphasis on one’s opinion; 'isn't it?', 'aren't you?', 'right?'.
points.long: The ～ではないか grammar point is used at the end of a sentence to make a rhetorical question or a strong, emphatic statement. It often translates as 'isn't it…?' 'aren't you…?' or 'wouldn’t you say…?'.

points.title: ～てはならない (〜te wa naranai)
points.meaning: Express prohibition; 'must not', 'cannot', 'should not'.
points.explanation: The ～てはならない grammar point is used to express a strong prohibition. It is often more formal or strict and can be translated as 'must not', 'cannot', or 'should not.'
points.short: Express prohibition; 'must not', 'cannot', 'should not'.
points.long: The ～てはならない grammar point is used to express a strong prohibition. It is often more formal or strict and can be translated as 'must not', 'cannot', or 'should not.'

points.title: ～てまで (〜te made)
points.meaning: Express the extent someone goes in order to achieve something; 'to the point of', 'even', 'so far as to'.
points.explanation: The ～てまで grammar point is used to convey the extent someone goes to achieve something, highlighting the action one takes or the sacrifice one makes for a certain purpose. It can be translated as 'to the point of', 'even', or 'so far as to' in English. It is used with verbs, not adjectives or nouns.
points.short: Express the extent someone goes in order to achieve something; 'to the point of', 'even', 'so far as to'.
points.long: The ～てまで grammar point is used to convey the extent someone goes to achieve something, highlighting the action one takes or the sacrifice one makes for a certain purpose. points.title: ～て当然だ (〜te tōzen da)

points.explanation: The ～て当然だ grammar point is used to express that something is natural, obvious, or expected under the circumstances. It can be translated as 'it's natural that', 'as expected', or 'no wonder' in English.

points.romaji: dō ni ka ~ nai mono ka
points.short: Express a strong desire or wish for something to be possible.
points.long: どうにか～ないものか is used to express a strong desire or wish for something to be resolved or made possible. It translates roughly as 'isn't there some way...?', 'can't we somehow...?', or 'is there no way...?'
formation: どうにか + Verb-negative form + ないものか

notes.nuance: The expression “どうにか～ないものか” is used to “express a strong desire or wish for something to be possible.” It is an important grammar point at the JLPT N2 level and is widely used in objective explanations and everyday conversation.

points.title: ～とおり (〜toori)
points.meaning: Express doing something as instructed or describing how something matches a rule or guideline; 'as', 'according to'.
points.explanation: The ～とおり grammar point is used to express doing something exactly as instructed or describing how something matches a guideline or is exactly as one heard/expected. It can be translated as 'as', 'according to', or 'the same way...'.
points.short: Express doing something as instructed or describing how something matches a rule or guideline; 'as', 'according to'.
points.long: The ～とおり grammar point is used to express doing something exactly as instructed or describing how something matches a guideline or is exactly as one heard/expected. It can be translated as 'as', 'according to', or 'the same way...'.

points.title: ～ところ (〜tokoro)
points.meaning: Express a specific point in time or state; 'when', 'just about', or 'in the middle of'.
points.explanation: The ～ところ grammar point is used to describe a specific point in time or stage of action. Depending on the verb tense, it can mean 'just about to do something', 'in the middle of doing something', or 'just did something'.

points.title: ～どころか (〜dokoro ka)

points.short: Express 'far from', 'not just', 'not only', or 'to say nothing of'.

points.title: ～ないことはない (〜nai koto wa nai)
points.meaning: Express that something is not impossible, meaning it is possible or could be done.
points.explanation: The ～ないことはない grammar point is used to express a double negative, meaning that something is not impossible, implying that it is possible or could be done. Essentially, it downplays the possibility or ability to do something but still acknowledges that it's possible.
points.short: Express that something is not impossible, meaning it is possible or could be done.
points.long: The ～ないことはない grammar point is used to express a double negative, meaning that something is not impossible, implying that it is possible or could be done. Essentially, it downplays the possibility or ability to do something but still acknowledges that it's possible.

notes.nuance: The expression “～ながら” is used to “express doing two things simultaneously or at the same time.” It is an important grammar point at the JLPT N2 level and is widely used in objective explanations and everyday conversation.
notes.contrast: When compared to other particles and conjunctive forms used in different contexts, “～ながら” has the characteristic of clearly indicating the speaker’s intention or focus.
notes.pitfalls: Please be careful not to make mistakes in conjugation when using the “nagara” construction (Verb-stem + ながら). It is important to use the dictionary form and the “te” form correctly and to choose the appropriate particles.

points.title: ～にあたり (〜ni atari)
points.meaning: Expresses the meaning of 'at the time of', 'in', 'on', or 'upon'.
points.explanation: The ～にあたり grammar point is used to describe an important event or situation that occurs at a specific moment. It can be translated as 'at the time of', 'in', 'on', or 'upon' in English. The formation is quite simple, as it only requires a noun before it.
points.short: Expresses the meaning of 'at the time of', 'in', 'on', or 'upon'.
points.long: The ～にあたり grammar point is used to describe an important event or situation that occurs at a specific moment. It can be translated as 'at the time of', 'in', 'on', or 'upon' in English. The formation is quite simple, as it only requires a noun before it.
formation: Noun + にあたり

examples.jp: 入学にあたり、必要な書類を準備してください。
examples.ja: 入学にあたり、必要な書類を準備してください。
examples.romaji: Nyuugaku ni atari, hitsuyou na shorui wo junbi shite kudasai.

examples.naturalEn: Please prepare the necessary documents for enrollment.

examples.jp: 新年にあたり、抱負を立てる人が多いです。
examples.ja: 新年にあたり、抱負を立てる人が多いです。

examples.literalEn: Many people set goals at the time of the new year.
examples.naturalEn: As the New Year approaches, many people make New Year’s resolutions.

examples.jp: 結婚にあたり、両家は大切な儀式を行います。

examples.naturalEn: In preparation for the wedding, both families hold an important ceremony.

examples.ja: 新しい仕事を始めるにあたり、準備が必要です。

examples.literalEn: In starting a new job, preparation is necessary.
examples.naturalEn: Starting a new job requires some preparation.

notes.nuance: The expression “～にあたり” means “at the time of,” “in,” “on,” or “upon.” It is an important grammar point at the JLPT N2 level and is widely used in objective explanations and everyday conversation.
notes.contrast: When compared to other particles and conjunctive forms used in context, “～にあたり” is characterized by its ability to clearly indicate the speaker’s intent and focus.
notes.pitfalls: Please be careful not to make mistakes in conjugation when using the “~ni atari” construction (Noun + ~ni atari). It is important to use the dictionary form and the “te” form correctly and to choose the appropriate particles.

points.title: ～において (〜ni oite)
points.meaning: Indicates the place, time, or context where an action or event occurs; 'in', 'at', 'on', 'regarding'.
points.explanation: The ～において grammar point is used to show the place, time, or context where an action or event takes place. It can be translated as 'in', 'at', 'on', or 'regarding' in English. It is often used in formal situations and can be replaced by more casual equivalents such as で, に, or は in informal contexts.
points.short: Indicates the place, time, or context where an action or event occurs; 'in', 'at', 'on', 'regarding'.
points.long: The ～において grammar point is used to show the place, time, or context where an action or event takes place. It can be translated as 'in', 'at', 'on', or 'regarding' in English. It is often used in formal situations and can be replaced by more casual equivalents such as で, に, or は in informal contexts.
formation: Noun + において

examples.jp: この大学において、英語のクラスが一番人気があります。
examples.ja: この大学において、英語のクラスが一番人気があります。
examples.romaji: Kono daigaku ni oite, eigo no kurasu ga ichiban ninki ga arimasu.

examples.literalEn: In this university, English classes are the most popular.
examples.naturalEn: At this university, English classes are the most popular.

examples.jp: 彼の研究において新しい発見がありました。
examples.ja: 彼の研究において新しい発見がありました。

examples.jp: 運動会において、彼は大活躍しました。

examples.romaji: Undoukai ni oite, kare wa daikatsuyaku shimashita.

examples.naturalEn: He did a great job at the sports festival.

examples.jp: 環境問題においては、みんなが責任を持って行動すべきです。
examples.ja: 環境問題においては、みんなが責任を持って行動すべきです。
examples.romaji: Kankyou mondai ni oite wa, minna ga sekinin wo motte koudou subeki desu.

examples.literalEn: Regarding environmental issues, everyone should take responsibility and act accordingly.
examples.naturalEn: When it comes to environmental issues, everyone should act responsibly.

examples.jp: それは未来において可能な選択肢の一つだ。
examples.ja: それは未来において可能な選択肢の一つだ。
examples.romaji: Sore wa mirai ni oite kanou na sentakushi no hitotsu da

examples.literalEn: That is one of the possible options in the future.
examples.naturalEn: That is one possible option for the future.

examples.naturalEn: It is important to master the basic grammar rules when learning English.

examples.jp: 裁判において、犯罪被疑者は自分の立場を弁護する権利がある。

examples.literalEn: By attending school, children make progress in knowledge and skills.
examples.naturalEn: By attending school, children make progress in their knowledge and skills.

notes.contrast: When compared to other particles and conjunctive forms used in context, “～において” has the characteristic of clearly indicating the speaker’s intent and focus.

points.title: ～にかかわらず (〜ni kakawarazu)
points.meaning: Regardless of; irrespective of; (often used as) 'whether or not'.
points.explanation: The ～にかかわらず grammar point is used to express that something happens or is true regardless of a particular fact, condition, or circumstance. It can be translated as 'regardless of', 'irrespective of', or 'whether or not'. It can be used with verbs, い-adjectives, な-adjectives, or nouns.
points.short: Regardless of; irrespective of; (often used as) 'whether or not'.
points.long: The ～にかかわらず grammar point is used to express that something happens or is true regardless of a particular fact, condition, or circumstance. It can be translated as 'regardless of', 'irrespective of', or 'whether or not'. It can be used with verbs, い-adjectives, な-adjectives, or nouns.
formation: Verb-dictionary form + にかかわらず, い-Adjective + にかかわらず, な-Adjective + にかかわらず, Noun + にかかわらず

examples.jp: 天気にかかわらず、今日の試合は行われます。
examples.ja: 天気にかかわらず、今日の試合は行われます。

examples.naturalEn: Regardless of the weather, today’s game will take place.

examples.jp: 彼は年齢にかかわらず、新しいことを学び続けています。

examples.naturalEn: Regardless of his age, he continues to learn new things.

examples.jp: その仕事が難しいかどうかにかかわらず、彼女は努力し続けた。
examples.ja: その仕事が難しいかどうかにかかわらず、彼女は努力し続けた。

points.title: ～にかけては (〜ni kakete wa)
points.meaning: Indicates a specific area or aspect in which someone or something excels.
points.explanation: The grammar point ～にかけては is used to emphasize a particular area or aspect in which someone or something excels or is exceptional. This structure is often used with positive connotations regarding the subject's expertise or outstanding qualities.
points.short: Indicates a specific area or aspect in which someone or something excels.
points.long: The grammar point ～にかけては is used to emphasize a particular area or aspect in which someone or something excels or is exceptional. This structure is often used with positive connotations regarding the subject's expertise or outstanding qualities.
formation: Noun + にかけては

examples.jp: 料理の腕前にかけては、彼女は誰にも負けません。
examples.ja: 料理の腕前にかけては、彼女は誰にも負けません。
examples.romaji: Ryouri no udemae ni kakete wa, kanojo wa dare ni mo makemasen.
examples.en: When it comes to cooking skills, she’s second to none.
examples.literalEn: When it comes to cooking skills, she is second to none.
examples.naturalEn: When it comes to cooking skills, she’s second to none.

examples.jp: この町にかけては、彼の店が一番おいしいラーメンを売っています。

examples.jp: 音楽の知識にかけては、彼は私たちの中で一番詳しいです。

notes.nuance: The expression “～にかけては” means “Indicates a specific area or aspect in which someone or something excels.” It is an important grammar point at the JLPT N2 level and is widely used in objective explanations and everyday conversation.
notes.contrast: When compared to other particles and conjunctive forms used in context, “～にかけては” is characterized by its ability to clearly indicate the speaker’s intent and focus.
notes.pitfalls: Please be careful not to make mistakes in conjugation when using the “~ni” construction (Noun + ni kake wa). It is important to use the dictionary form, the “te” form, and the correct particles accurately.

points.title: ～にしたがって (〜ni shitagatte)
points.meaning: Expresses a natural consequence or a change that occurs according to something else; 'as', 'with', 'in accordance with'.
points.explanation: The ～にしたがって grammar point is used to express a natural consequence or a change that occurs according to something else. It can be translated as 'as', 'with', or 'in accordance with' in English. This grammar point is used with nouns and can be used to show a change in proportion or in accordance with a rule or principle.
points.short: Expresses a natural consequence or a change that occurs according to something else; 'as', 'with', 'in accordance with'.
points.long: The ～にしたがって grammar point is used to express a natural consequence or a change that occurs according to something else. It can be translated as 'as', 'with', or 'in accordance with' in English. This grammar point is used with nouns and can be used to show a change in proportion or in accordance with a rule or principle.
formation: Noun + にしたがって

examples.jp: 成長にしたがって、この植物の葉が大きくなります。

examples.jp: 説明書にしたがって、家具を組み立ててください。

examples.literalEn: It is common for the heart rate to increase with exercise.
examples.naturalEn: It is common for heart rate to increase during exercise.

notes.nuance: The expression “～にしたがって” means “Expresses a natural consequence or a change that occurs according to something else; ‘as,’ ‘with,’ ‘in accordance with.’” It is an important grammar point at the JLPT N2 level and is widely used in objective explanations and everyday conversation.
notes.contrast: When compared to other particles and conjunctive forms used in context, “～にしたがって” has the characteristic of clearly indicating the speaker’s intention or focus.
notes.pitfalls: Please be careful not to make mistakes in conjugation when using the “-ni-shite” construction (Noun + -ni-shite). It is important to use the dictionary form, the “-te” form, and the correct particles accurately.

points.title: ～にしたら (〜ni shitara)
points.meaning: Express a point of view; 'from the perspective of', 'if I were'.
points.explanation: The ～にしたら grammar point is used to express a point of view or opinion from someone else's perspective. It can be translated as 'from the perspective of' or 'if I were' in English. The formation differs depending on whether it is used with a noun or a pronoun.
points.short: Express a point of view; 'from the perspective of', 'if I were'.
points.long: The ～にしたら grammar point is used to express a point of view or opinion from someone else's perspective. It can be translated as 'from the perspective of' or 'if I were' in English. The formation differs depending on whether it is used with a noun or a pronoun.
formation: Noun + にしたら, Pronoun + にしたら

points.title: ～にしろ～にしろ (〜ni shiro 〜ni shiro)
points.meaning: Expresses 'either way', 'in any case', 'be it...', used when presenting two alternatives.
points.explanation: The ～にしろ～にしろ grammar point is used to present two alternatives and emphasize that regardless of which one is chosen or occurs, the result or conclusion remains the same. It can be translated as 'either way', 'in any case', or 'be it...'. The formation differs depending on whether it is used with a verb, い-adjective, な-adjective, or noun.
points.short: Expresses 'either way', 'in any case', 'be it...', used when presenting two alternatives.

points.title: ～につけ～につけ (〜ni tsuke 〜ni tsuke)
points.meaning: Expresses 'whenever', 'each time', 'whether...or'.
points.explanation: The ～につけ～につけ grammar point is used to express that something happens 'each time' or 'whenever' a certain event or situation occurs, and can also mean 'whether...or'. points.short: Expresses 'whenever', 'each time', 'whether...or'.
points.long: The ～につけ～につけ grammar point is used to express that something happens 'each time' or 'whenever' a certain event or situation occurs, and can also mean 'whether...or'. This grammar point indicates that the same event or feeling occurs no matter which of the following situations happen.

points.title: ～につれて (〜ni tsurete)
points.meaning: Expresses the idea that as one thing changes, so does another; 'as', 'along with', 'while'.
points.explanation: The ～につれて grammar point is used to express the idea that as one thing changes or progresses, another thing changes or progresses simultaneously. In English, it can be translated as 'as', 'along with', or 'while'.
points.short: Expresses the idea that as one thing changes, so does another; 'as', 'along with', 'while'.
points.long: The ～につれて grammar point is used to express the idea that as one thing changes or progresses, another thing changes or progresses simultaneously. In English, it can be translated as 'as', 'along with', or 'while'.

points.meaning: Expresses 'along with' or 'as a result of'; indicates that one event occurs along with another.
