examples.romaji: Ame ga futteiru ni mo kakawarazu, kanojo wa sanpo ni ikimashita.
examples.en: Even though it was raining, she went for a walk.
examples.literalEn: Even though it was raining, she went for a walk.
examples.naturalEn: Even though it was raining, she went for a walk.

examples.jp: 車が古いにもかかわらず、まだよく走ります。
examples.ja: 車が古いにもかかわらず、まだよく走ります。
examples.romaji: Kuruma ga furui ni mo kakawarazu, mada yoku hashirimasu.
examples.en: Even though the car is old, it still runs well.
examples.literalEn: In spite of the car being old, it still runs well.
examples.naturalEn: Even though the car is old, it still runs well.

examples.jp: 結果が良くないにもかかわらず、彼は頑張り続けました。
examples.ja: 結果が良くないにもかかわらず、彼は頑張り続けました。
examples.romaji: Kekka ga yoku nai ni mo kakawarazu, kare wa ganbari tsuzukemashita.
examples.en: Despite his poor results, he kept trying his best.
chunks: 良くないにもかかわらず、
examples.literalEn: Despite the results not being good, he continued to do his best.
examples.naturalEn: Despite his poor results, he kept trying his best.

examples.jp: 努力にもかかわらず、敵に敗れた。
examples.ja: 努力にもかかわらず、敵に敗れた。
examples.romaji: Doryoku ni mo kakawarazu, teki ni yabureta
examples.en: Despite their best efforts, they were defeated by the enemy.
examples.literalEn: Despite my efforts, I was defeated by my opponent.
examples.naturalEn: Despite their best efforts, they were defeated by the enemy.

notes.nuance: The expression “～にもかかわらず” means “despite,” “in spite of,” or “even though.” It is an important grammar point at the JLPT N2 level and is widely used in objective explanations and everyday conversation.
notes.contrast: When compared to other particles and conjunctive forms used in different contexts, “～にもかかわらず” has the characteristic of clearly indicating the speaker’s intent or focus.
notes.pitfalls: Please be careful of conjugation errors in the "-nara" construction (Verb (any tense/form) + "ni wa aru koto ni mo," "i-adjective" + "ni wa aru koto ni mo," "na-adjective" (or noun) + "de aru ni wa aru koto ni mo"). It is important to use the dictionary form or "te" form correctly and choose the appropriate particles.

points.title: ～により (〜ni yori)
points.meaning: Indicates the reason, method, or means by which something happens; 'by', 'through', 'due to'.
points.explanation: The ～により grammar point is used to indicate the reason, method, or means by which something happens or is done. It can be often translated as 'by', 'through', or 'due to' in English. It can be attached directly to nouns or verbs in plain form.
points.short: Indicates the reason, method, or means by which something happens; 'by', 'through', 'due to'.
points.long: The ～により grammar point is used to indicate the reason, method, or means by which something happens or is done. It can be often translated as 'by', 'through', or 'due to' in English. It can be attached directly to nouns or verbs in plain form.
formation: Noun + により, Verb + により

examples.jp: この事故は運転手の不注意により起こりました。
examples.ja: この事故は運転手の不注意により起こりました。
examples.romaji: Kono jiko wa untenshu no fuchuui ni yori okorimashita.
examples.en: This accident was caused by the driver’s carelessness.

cloze.before: この事故は運転手の不注意

examples.literalEn: This accident occurred due to the driver's carelessness.
examples.naturalEn: This accident was caused by the driver’s carelessness.

examples.jp: その映画は小説により制作されました。
examples.ja: その映画は小説により制作されました。
examples.romaji: Sono eiga wa shousetsu ni yori seisaku saremashita.
examples.en: That movie was based on a novel.
examples.literalEn: The movie was produced based on the novel.
examples.naturalEn: That movie was based on a novel.

examples.jp: 犯人は警察により逮捕されました。
examples.ja: 犯人は警察により逮捕されました。
examples.romaji: Hannin wa keisatsu ni yori taiho saremashita.
examples.en: The suspect was arrested by the police.
examples.literalEn: The criminal was arrested by the police.
examples.naturalEn: The suspect was arrested by the police.

examples.jp: 会社の成長は従業員の努力により実現しました。
examples.ja: 会社の成長は従業員の努力により実現しました。
examples.romaji: Kaisha no seichou wa juugyouin no doryoku ni yori jitsugen shimashita.
examples.en: The company’s growth was made possible by the efforts of its employees.

cloze.before: 会社の成長は従業員の努力

examples.literalEn: The company's growth was achieved through the efforts of its employees.
examples.naturalEn: The company’s growth was made possible by the efforts of its employees.

examples.jp: 農家は、病害虫により畑の作物がすべて枯れたことに大変苦しんでいる。
examples.ja: 農家は、病害虫により畑の作物がすべて枯れたことに大変苦しんでいる。
examples.romaji: Nouka wa, byougaichuu ni yori hatake no sakumotsu ga subete kareta koto ni taihen kurushinde iru
examples.en: Farmers are suffering greatly because pests and diseases have caused all the crops in their fields to wither.

cloze.after: 畑の作物がすべて枯れたことに大変苦しんでいる。

examples.literalEn: Farmers are suffering greatly as all their crops in the field have withered due to pests and diseases.
examples.naturalEn: Farmers are suffering greatly because pests and diseases have caused all the crops in their fields to wither.

examples.jp: それにより、品質の高い製品ができあがることが期待できる。
examples.ja: それにより、品質の高い製品ができあがることが期待できる。
examples.romaji: Sore ni yori, hinshitsu no takai seihin ga dekiagaru koto ga kitai dekiru.
examples.en: As a result, we can expect to produce high-quality products.

cloze.after: 、品質の高い製品ができあがることが期待できる。

examples.literalEn: As a result, it is expected that high-quality products will be produced.
examples.naturalEn: As a result, we can expect to produce high-quality products.

examples.jp: インターネットの普及により情報にアクセスしやすくなった。
examples.ja: インターネットの普及により情報にアクセスしやすくなった。
examples.romaji: Intaanetto no fukyuu ni yori jouhou ni akusesu shiyasu kunatta
examples.en: The spread of the Internet has made it easier to access information.

cloze.before: インターネットの普及
cloze.after: 情報にアクセスしやすくなった。

examples.literalEn: The popularization of the Internet has made it easier to access information.
examples.naturalEn: The spread of the Internet has made it easier to access information.

examples.jp: 映画の評価は個人の好みによりますので、ネット上の評価だけを頼りにしないでください。
examples.ja: 映画の評価は個人の好みによりますので、ネット上の評価だけを頼りにしないでください。
examples.romaji: Eiga no hyouka wa kojin no konomi ni yorimasu node, nettojou no hyouka dake o tayori ni shinaide kudasai.
examples.en: Since opinions on movies vary depending on personal taste, please do not rely solely on online reviews.

cloze.before: 映画の評価は個人の好み
cloze.after: ますので、ネット上の評価だけを頼りにしないでください。

examples.literalEn: Movie ratings depend on personal preferences, so please don't rely solely on online ratings.
examples.naturalEn: Since opinions on movies vary depending on personal taste, please do not rely solely on online reviews.

notes.nuance: The expression “～により” indicates the reason, method, or means by which something happens; it translates to “by,” “through,” or “due to.” This is an important grammar point at the JLPT N2 level and is widely used in objective explanations and everyday conversation.
notes.contrast: When compared to other particles and conjunctive forms used in different contexts, “～により” is characterized by its ability to clearly indicate the speaker’s intent and focus.
notes.pitfalls: Please be careful not to make mistakes in conjugation when using the “by” construction (Noun + により, Verb + により). It is important to use the dictionary form and the “te” form correctly and to choose the appropriate particles.

points.title: ～にわたって (〜ni watatte)
points.meaning: Indicates a range or extent; 'over', 'throughout', 'across'.
points.explanation: The ～にわたって grammar point is used to express a range or extent of a particular action, event, or situation. It can be translated as 'over', 'throughout', or 'across' in English. This structure can be used with various types of words such as time, distance, and quantity.
points.short: Indicates a range or extent; 'over', 'throughout', 'across'.
points.long: The ～にわたって grammar point is used to express a range or extent of a particular action, event, or situation. It can be translated as 'over', 'throughout', or 'across' in English. This structure can be used with various types of words such as time, distance, and quantity.
formation: Noun + にわたって

examples.jp: 彼女は一年にわたって日本語を勉強しました。
examples.ja: 彼女は一年にわたって日本語を勉強しました。
examples.romaji: Kanojo wa ichinen ni watatte nihongo wo benkyou shimashita.
examples.en: She studied Japanese for a year.

cloze.after: 日本語を勉強しました。

examples.literalEn: She studied Japanese for over a year.
examples.naturalEn: She studied Japanese for a year.

examples.jp: このプロジェクトは50キロにわたって道路を建設します。
examples.ja: このプロジェクトは50キロにわたって道路を建設します。
examples.romaji: Kono purojekuto wa gojukiro ni watatte douro wo kensetsu shimasu.
examples.en: This project will construct a road spanning 50 kilometers.

cloze.before: このプロジェクトは50キロ

examples.literalEn: This project will construct roads across 50 kilometers.
examples.naturalEn: This project will construct a road spanning 50 kilometers.

examples.jp: 彼の著作は数多くの国にわたって読まれている。
examples.ja: 彼の著作は数多くの国にわたって読まれている。
examples.romaji: Kare no chosaku wa kazu ooku no kuni ni watatte yomarete iru.
examples.en: His works are read in many countries.

cloze.before: 彼の著作は数多くの国

examples.literalEn: His writings are read throughout numerous countries.
examples.naturalEn: His works are read in many countries.

examples.jp: その秘密は世代にわたって保たれ続けた。
examples.ja: その秘密は世代にわたって保たれ続けた。
examples.romaji: Sono himitsu wa sedai ni watatte tamotsu sareta.
examples.en: That secret has been preserved for generations.
examples.literalEn: The secret was kept over generations.
examples.naturalEn: That secret has been preserved for generations.

notes.nuance: The expression “～にわたって” means “Indicates a range or extent; ‘over,’ ‘throughout,’ ‘across.’” It is an important grammar point at the JLPT N2 level and is widely used in objective explanations and everyday conversation.
notes.contrast: When compared to other particles and conjunctive forms used in context, “～にわたって” has the characteristic of clearly indicating the speaker’s intent and focus.
notes.pitfalls: Please be careful not to make mistakes in conjugation when using the “ni-watte” construction (Noun + ni-watte). It is important to use the dictionary form and the “te” form correctly and to choose the appropriate particles.

points.title: ～に先立ち (〜ni sakidachi)
points.meaning: Express an action or event that occurs before another; 'before', 'prior to', 'preceding'.
points.explanation: The ～に先立ち grammar point is used to indicate that a certain action or event occurs before another action or event. It can be translated as 'before', 'prior to', or 'preceding' in English. It is often used with nouns (Noun + に先立ち) or with dictionary-form verbs (Verb-dictionary form + に先立って).
points.short: Express an action or event that occurs before another; 'before', 'prior to', 'preceding'.
points.long: The ～に先立ち grammar point is used to indicate that a certain action or event occurs before another action or event. It can be translated as 'before', 'prior to', or 'preceding' in English. It is often used with nouns (Noun + に先立ち) or with dictionary-form verbs (Verb-dictionary form + に先立って).
formation: Noun + に先立ち / Verb-dictionary form + に先立って

examples.jp: 会議に先立ち、資料を確認しましょう。
examples.ja: 会議に先立ち、資料を確認しましょう。
examples.romaji: Kaigi ni sakidachi, shiryou wo kakunin shimashou.
examples.en: Let’s review the materials before the meeting.
examples.literalEn: Before the meeting, let's check the materials.
examples.naturalEn: Let’s review the materials before the meeting.

examples.jp: 出発に先立ち、荷物を整理しました。
examples.ja: 出発に先立ち、荷物を整理しました。
examples.romaji: Shuppatsu ni sakidachi, nimotsu wo seiri shimashita.
examples.en: Before leaving, I packed my bags.
examples.literalEn: Before departure, I organized my luggage.
examples.naturalEn: Before leaving, I packed my bags.

examples.jp: 就寝に先立ち、歯を磨きます。
examples.ja: 就寝に先立ち、歯を磨きます。
examples.romaji: Shuushin ni sakidachi, ha wo migakimasu.
examples.en: I brush my teeth before going to bed.
examples.literalEn: Before going to bed, I brush my teeth.
examples.naturalEn: I brush my teeth before going to bed.

examples.jp: 映画の上映に先立ち、予告編が放映されます。
examples.ja: 映画の上映に先立ち、予告編が放映されます。
examples.romaji: Eiga no jouei ni sakidachi, yokokuhen ga houei saremasu.
examples.en: A trailer will be shown before the movie begins.
examples.literalEn: Before the movie screening, the trailers are shown.
examples.naturalEn: A trailer will be shown before the movie begins.

notes.nuance: The expression “～に先立ち” means “to express an action or event that occurs before another; ‘before,’ ‘prior to,’ ‘preceding.’” It is an important grammar point at the JLPT N2 level and is widely used in objective explanations and everyday conversation.
notes.contrast: When compared to other particles and conjunctive forms used in context, “～に先立ち” has the characteristic of clearly indicating the speaker’s intent and focus.
notes.pitfalls: Please be careful to avoid mistakes in conjugation when using the “ni-saki” construction (Noun + ni-saki / Verb-dictionary form + ni-saki). It is important to use the dictionary form and “te” form correctly and to choose the appropriate particles.

points.title: ～に反して (〜ni hanshite)
points.meaning: Contrary to, against, in spite of
points.explanation: The ～に反して grammar point is used to express that something is contrary to or against an expectation or belief. It can be translated as 'contrary to', 'against', or 'in spite of' in English. It is generally used with nouns.
points.short: Contrary to, against, in spite of
points.long: The ～に反して grammar point is used to express that something is contrary to or against an expectation or belief. It can be translated as 'contrary to', 'against', or 'in spite of' in English. It is generally used with nouns.
formation: Noun + に反して

examples.jp: 天気予報に反して、今日は雨が降っている。
examples.ja: 天気予報に反して、今日は雨が降っている。
examples.romaji: Tenki yohou ni hanshite, kyou wa ame ga futte iru.
examples.en: Contrary to the weather forecast, it’s raining today.
examples.literalEn: Contrary to the weather forecast, it is raining today.
examples.naturalEn: Contrary to the weather forecast, it’s raining today.

examples.jp: 彼の予想に反して、試合に勝った。
examples.ja: 彼の予想に反して、試合に勝った。
examples.romaji: Kare no yosou ni hanshite, shiai ni katta.
examples.en: Contrary to his expectations, they won the match.
examples.literalEn: We won the match against his prediction.
examples.naturalEn: Contrary to his expectations, they won the match.

examples.jp: 両親の意見に反して、彼と結婚した。
examples.ja: 両親の意見に反して、彼と結婚した。
examples.romaji: Ryoushin no iken ni hanshite, kare to kekkon shita.
examples.en: I married him against my parents’ wishes.
examples.literalEn: I married him against my parents' opinion.
examples.naturalEn: I married him against my parents’ wishes.

examples.jp: この映画は批評家の評価に反して大ヒットした。
examples.ja: この映画は批評家の評価に反して大ヒットした。
examples.romaji: Kono eiga wa hihyouka no hyouka ni hanshite daihitto shita.
examples.en: Contrary to critics' reviews, this movie was a huge hit.

cloze.before: この映画は批評家の評価

examples.literalEn: This movie became a big hit contrary to the critics' ratings.
examples.naturalEn: Contrary to critics' reviews, this movie was a huge hit.

examples.jp: そのチームは予想に反して優勝しました。
examples.ja: そのチームは予想に反して優勝しました。
examples.romaji: Sono chiimu wa yosou ni hanshite yuushou shimashita.
examples.en: Contrary to expectations, that team won the championship.
examples.literalEn: Contrary to expectations, the team was able to win the championship.
examples.naturalEn: Contrary to expectations, that team won the championship.

notes.nuance: The expression “～に反して” means “contrary to, against, or in spite of.” It is an important grammar point at the JLPT N2 level and is widely used in objective explanations and everyday conversation.
notes.contrast: When compared to other particles and conjunctive forms used in different contexts, “～に反して” is characterized by its ability to clearly indicate the speaker’s intent or focus.
notes.pitfalls: Please be careful of mistakes in conjugation when using the “ni” particle (Noun + ni hanoshite). It is important to use the dictionary form, the “te” form, and the correct particles accurately.

points.title: ～に基づいて (〜ni motozuite)
points.meaning: Based on, according to, depending on
points.explanation: The ～に基づいて grammar point is used to express that something is based on, according to, or depending on a certain source or foundation. It can be used with nouns that represent a source, rule, principle, or standard.
points.short: Based on, according to, depending on
points.long: The ～に基づいて grammar point is used to express that something is based on, according to, or depending on a certain source or foundation. It can be used with nouns that represent a source, rule, principle, or standard.
formation: Noun + に基づいて

examples.jp: 研究結果に基づいて、新しい治療法が開発されました。
examples.ja: 研究結果に基づいて、新しい治療法が開発されました。
examples.romaji: Kenkyuu kekka ni motozuite, atarashii chiryouhou ga kaihatsu saremashita.
examples.en: Based on the research results, a new treatment was developed.

cloze.after: 、新しい治療法が開発されました。

examples.literalEn: A new treatment method was developed based on the research results.
examples.naturalEn: Based on the research results, a new treatment was developed.

examples.jp: 法律に基づいて、犯罪者は逮捕されました。
examples.ja: 法律に基づいて、犯罪者は逮捕されました。
examples.romaji: Houritsu ni motozuite, hanzaisha wa taiho saremashita.
examples.en: In accordance with the law, the criminal was arrested.
examples.literalEn: The criminal was arrested according to the law.
examples.naturalEn: In accordance with the law, the criminal was arrested.

examples.jp: そのデータに基づいて、結論を出すことができます。
examples.ja: そのデータに基づいて、結論を出すことができます。
examples.romaji: Sono deeta ni motozuite, ketsuron o dasu koto ga dekimasu.
examples.en: Based on that data, we can draw a conclusion.

cloze.after: 、結論を出すことができます。

examples.literalEn: We can draw conclusions based on that data.
examples.naturalEn: Based on that data, we can draw a conclusion.

examples.jp: お客様の要望に基づいて、商品の改善が行われます。
examples.ja: お客様の要望に基づいて、商品の改善が行われます。
examples.romaji: Okyakusama no youbou ni motozuite, shouhin no kaizen ga okonawaremasu.
examples.en: Product improvements are made based on customer feedback.
examples.literalEn: Product improvements will be made based on customer requests.
examples.naturalEn: Product improvements are made based on customer feedback.

examples.jp: わたしたちのチームはフィードバックに基づいて変更案を提案します。
examples.ja: わたしたちのチームはフィードバックに基づいて変更案を提案します。
examples.romaji: Watashitachi no chiimu wa fiidobakku ni motozuite henkouan o teian shimasu.
examples.en: Our team will propose changes based on the feedback.

cloze.before: わたしたちのチームはフィードバック

examples.literalEn: Our team proposes changes based on feedback.
examples.naturalEn: Our team will propose changes based on the feedback.

notes.nuance: The expression “～に基づいて” means “Based on, according to, or depending on.” It is an important grammar point at the JLPT N2 level and is widely used in objective explanations and everyday conversation.
notes.contrast: When compared to other particles and conjunctive forms used in context, “～に基づいて” has the characteristic of clearly indicating the speaker’s intent or focus.
notes.pitfalls: Please be careful of mistakes in conjugation when using the “based on” construction (Noun + ni kite). It is important to use the dictionary form and the “te” form correctly and to choose the appropriate particles.

points.title: ～に対して (〜ni taishite)
points.meaning: Expresses 'toward', 'against', 'in contrast to', or 'in response to'.
points.explanation: The ～に対して grammar point is used to indicate a direction or target, showing an action or attitude towards something or someone. It can also be used to show a contrast between two situations or to express 'in response to' an action or situation.
points.short: Expresses 'toward', 'against', 'in contrast to', or 'in response to'.
points.long: The ～に対して grammar point is used to indicate a direction or target, showing an action or attitude towards something or someone. It can also be used to show a contrast between two situations or to express 'in response to' an action or situation.
formation: Noun + に対して

examples.jp: 日本の文化に対して尊敬の念を持っています。
examples.ja: 日本の文化に対して尊敬の念を持っています。
examples.romaji: Nihon no bunka ni taishite sonkei no nen wo motte imasu.
examples.en: I have great respect for Japanese culture.

cloze.after: 尊敬の念を持っています。

examples.literalEn: I have a sense of respect towards Japanese culture.
examples.naturalEn: I have great respect for Japanese culture.

examples.jp: 彼に対して無礼な態度を取らないでください。
examples.ja: 彼に対して無礼な態度を取らないでください。
examples.romaji: Kare ni taishite burei na taido wo toranaide kudasai.
examples.en: Please do not be rude to him.

cloze.after: 無礼な態度を取らないでください。

examples.literalEn: Please don't have a rude attitude towards him.
examples.naturalEn: Please do not be rude to him.

examples.jp: 先生の質問に対して、彼女はすぐに答えました。
examples.ja: 先生の質問に対して、彼女はすぐに答えました。
examples.romaji: Sensei no shitsumon ni taishite, kanojo wa sugu ni kotaemashita.
examples.en: She answered the teacher’s question right away.
examples.literalEn: In response to the teacher's question, she answered immediately.
examples.naturalEn: She answered the teacher’s question right away.

examples.jp: 男性に対して、女性は同じ仕事でも低い給料をもらっている。
examples.ja: 男性に対して、女性は同じ仕事でも低い給料をもらっている。
examples.romaji: Dansei ni taishite, josei wa onaji shigoto demo hikui kyuuryou wo moratte iru.
examples.en: Compared to men, women receive lower pay for the same work.

cloze.after: 、女性は同じ仕事でも低い給料をもらっている。

examples.literalEn: In contrast to men, women receive lower salaries for the same job.
examples.naturalEn: Compared to men, women receive lower pay for the same work.

examples.jp: 貧しい人々に対して助けを差し伸べるのは、私たちの責任です。
examples.ja: 貧しい人々に対して助けを差し伸べるのは、私たちの責任です。
examples.romaji: Mazushii hitobito ni tai shite tasuke o sashinoberu no wa, watashitachi no sekinin desu.
examples.en: It is our responsibility to extend a helping hand to the poor.

cloze.after: 助けを差し伸べるのは、私たちの責任です。

examples.literalEn: It is our responsibility to reach out and help the poor.
examples.naturalEn: It is our responsibility to extend a helping hand to the poor.

examples.jp: 彼女は自分の意見に対して頑固で譲らない。
examples.ja: 彼女は自分の意見に対して頑固で譲らない。
examples.romaji: Kanojo wa jibun no iken ni taishite ganko de yuzuranai
examples.en: She is stubborn about her opinions and won’t budge.
examples.literalEn: She is stubborn and won't compromise on her opinions.
examples.naturalEn: She is stubborn about her opinions and won’t budge.

examples.jp: 彼女の態度に対して、彼の気持ちが冷め始めた。
examples.ja: 彼女の態度に対して、彼の気持ちが冷め始めた。
examples.romaji: Kanojo no taido ni tai shite, kare no kimochi ga same hajimeta.

examples.romaji: Saikin, shigoto no shippai bakari da.
examples.en: Lately, I’ve been making nothing but mistakes at work.
examples.literalEn: Lately, it’s just been one failure at work after another.
examples.naturalEn: Lately, I’ve been making nothing but mistakes at work.

examples.jp: 彼が言った言葉は、どれも恐ろしいことばかりだった。
examples.ja: 彼が言った言葉は、どれも恐ろしいことばかりだった。
examples.romaji: Kare ga itta kotoba wa, doremo osoroshii koto bakari datta.
examples.en: Everything he said was terrifying.

cloze.before: 彼が言った言葉は、どれも恐ろしいこと

examples.literalEn: Everything he said was nothing but frightening.
examples.naturalEn: Everything he said was terrifying.

examples.jp: あの洋服店で買える服は、今シーズンはやっているデザインばかりだ。
examples.ja: あの洋服店で買える服は、今シーズンはやっているデザインばかりだ。
examples.romaji: Ano youfuku ten de kaeru fuku wa, kono shiizun hayatte iru dezain bakari da
examples.en: The clothes available at that clothing store are all this season’s trendy designs.

cloze.before: あの洋服店で買える服は、今シーズンはやっているデザイン

examples.literalEn: The clothes you can buy at that clothing store are all the designs that are in fashion this season.
examples.naturalEn: The clothes available at that clothing store are all this season’s trendy designs.

notes.nuance: The expression “～ばかりだ” is used to “express a continuing state or negative tendency; ‘just,’ ‘only,’ ‘always.’” It is an important grammar point at the JLPT N2 level and is widely used in objective explanations and everyday conversation.
notes.contrast: When compared to other particles and conjunctive forms used in context, “～ばかりだ” is characterized by its ability to clearly indicate the speaker’s intent and focus.
notes.pitfalls: Please be careful of conjugation errors in the "-bakkira" construction (Verb -te-form + -bakkira, -i-adjective + -bakkira, -na-adjective + -bakkira, Noun + -bakkira). It is important to use the dictionary form or -te-form correctly and choose the appropriate particles.

points.title: ～ばかりに (〜bakari ni)
points.meaning: Express an undesired situation or result caused by something; 'simply because', 'due to', 'on account of'.
points.explanation: The ～ばかりに grammar point is used to express an undesired situation or result that arises simply because of some factor. It can be translated as 'simply because', 'due to', or 'on account of' in English. The formation differs depending on whether it is used with a verb, い-adjective, な-adjective, or noun.
points.short: Express an undesired situation or result caused by something; 'simply because', 'due to', 'on account of'.
points.long: The ～ばかりに grammar point is used to express an undesired situation or result that arises simply because of some factor. It can be translated as 'simply because', 'due to', or 'on account of' in English. The formation differs depending on whether it is used with a verb, い-adjective, な-adjective, or noun.
formation: Verb-casual + ばかりに, い-Adjective + ばかりに, な-Adjective + なばかりに, Noun + なばかりに

examples.jp: 雨が降ったばかりに、試合が中止になりました。
examples.ja: 雨が降ったばかりに、試合が中止になりました。
examples.romaji: Ame ga futta bakari ni, shiai ga chuushi ni narimashita.
examples.en: The game was canceled because it had just rained.
examples.literalEn: Simply because it rained, the match was cancelled.
examples.naturalEn: The game was canceled because it had just rained.

examples.jp: 彼が遅れたばかりに、私たちも遅刻しました。
examples.ja: 彼が遅れたばかりに、私たちも遅刻しました。
examples.romaji: Kare ga okureta bakari ni, watashitachi mo chikoku shimashita.
examples.en: Just because he was late, we were late too.
examples.literalEn: Because he was late, we ended up being late too.
examples.naturalEn: Just because he was late, we were late too.

examples.jp: 忘れ物をしたばかりに、買い物に戻らなければなりません。
examples.ja: 忘れ物をしたばかりに、買い物に戻らなければなりません。
examples.romaji: Wasuremono wo shita bakari ni, kaimono ni modoranakereba narimasen.
examples.en: Just because I forgot something, I have to go back to the store.

cloze.after: 、買い物に戻らなければなりません。

examples.literalEn: Simply because I forgot something, I have to go back to the store.
examples.naturalEn: Just because I forgot something, I have to go back to the store.

examples.jp: 彼女が美人なばかりに、みんなが彼女を羨んでいます。
examples.ja: 彼女が美人なばかりに、みんなが彼女を羨んでいます。
examples.romaji: Kanojo ga bijin na bakari ni, minna ga kanojo wo urayande imasu.
examples.en: Everyone envies her simply because she is so beautiful.

cloze.after: 、みんなが彼女を羨んでいます。

examples.literalEn: Just because she is beautiful, everyone is envious of her.
examples.naturalEn: Everyone envies her simply because she is so beautiful.

notes.nuance: The expression “～ばかりに” means “to express an undesired situation or result caused by something; ‘simply because,’ ‘due to,’ ‘on account of.’” It is an important grammar point at the JLPT N2 level and is widely used in objective explanations and everyday conversation.
notes.contrast: Compared to other particles and conjunctive forms used in context, “～ばかりに” has the characteristic of clearly indicating the speaker’s intention or focus.
notes.pitfalls: Please be careful of conjugation errors in the "tsunage" construction (Verb-casual + ばかりに, i-adjective + ばかりに, na-adjective + なばかりに, noun + なばかりに). It is important to use the dictionary form or "te" form correctly and choose the appropriate particles.

points.title: ～ば～というものでもない (〜ba 〜to iu mono demo nai)
points.meaning: Not necessarily true that if A, then B.
points.explanation: The ～ば～というものでもない grammar point is used to express that something is not necessarily true even if a certain condition is met. In other words, if A happens, it doesn't always mean B will happen.
points.short: Not necessarily true that if A, then B.
points.long: The ～ば～というものでもない grammar point is used to express that something is not necessarily true even if a certain condition is met. In other words, if A happens, it doesn't always mean B will happen.
formation: Verb-ば form + というものでもない

examples.jp: 高いものがいいものばかりではない。
examples.ja: 高いものがいいものばかりではない。
examples.romaji: Takai mono ga ii mono bakari de wa nai.
examples.en: Expensive things aren’t always the best.
examples.literalEn: Expensive things are not always good.
examples.naturalEn: Expensive things aren’t always the best.

examples.jp: 英語ができれば、成功するというものでもない。
examples.ja: 英語ができれば、成功するというものでもない。
examples.romaji: Eigo ga dekireba, seikou suru to iu mono demo nai.
examples.en: Being able to speak English doesn’t necessarily guarantee success.

cloze.before: 英語ができれば、成功する

examples.literalEn: Just because you can speak English doesn’t mean you’ll succeed.
examples.naturalEn: Being able to speak English doesn’t necessarily guarantee success.

examples.jp: 見た目が美しいからといって、心も美しいというものでもない。
examples.ja: 見た目が美しいからといって、心も美しいというものでもない。
examples.romaji: Mitame ga utsukushii kara to itte, kokoro mo utsukushii to iu mono demo nai.
examples.en: Just because someone is beautiful on the outside doesn’t mean they’re beautiful on the inside.
chunks: 美しいというものでも

cloze.before: 見た目が美しいからといって、心も美しい

examples.literalEn: Just because someone is beautiful on the outside, it doesn’t mean they’re beautiful on the inside.
examples.naturalEn: Just because someone is beautiful on the outside doesn’t mean they’re beautiful on the inside.

examples.jp: 有名大学に入れば、将来が安泰だというものでもない。
examples.ja: 有名大学に入れば、将来が安泰だというものでもない。
examples.romaji: Yuumei daigaku ni haireba, shourai ga antai da to iu mono demo nai.
examples.en: Just because you get into a prestigious university doesn’t mean your future is guaranteed.
chunks: 安泰だというものでも

cloze.before: 有名大学に入れば、将来が安泰だ

examples.literalEn: Getting into a famous university doesn’t guarantee a secure future.
examples.naturalEn: Just because you get into a prestigious university doesn’t mean your future is guaranteed.

notes.nuance: The expression “～ば～というものでもない” means “It is not necessarily true that if A, then B.” This is an important grammar point at the JLPT N2 level and is widely used in objective explanations and everyday conversation.
notes.contrast: When compared to other particles and conjunctive forms used in different contexts, “～ば～というものでもない” is characterized by its ability to clearly convey the speaker’s intent and focus.
notes.pitfalls: Please be careful of conjugation errors in the "ba" form (Verb-ba form + "to iu mono mo nai"). It is important to use the dictionary form and "te" form correctly and to choose the appropriate particles.

points.title: ～はともかく～は (〜wa tomokaku 〜wa)
points.meaning: Used to compare or contrast two elements; 'as for...'.
points.explanation: The grammar point ～はともかく～は is used to compare or contrast two elements in a sentence. It implies that the first element can be set aside or is less important compared to the second element. It often translates to 'putting A aside, B...'.
points.short: Used to compare or contrast two elements; 'as for...'.
points.long: The grammar point ～はともかく～は is used to compare or contrast two elements in a sentence. It implies that the first element can be set aside or is less important compared to the second element. It often translates to 'putting A aside, B...'.
formation: Noun1 はともかく Noun2 は

examples.jp: デザインはともかく、機能はこの携帯電話が一番です。
examples.ja: デザインはともかく、機能はこの携帯電話が一番です。
examples.romaji: Dezain wa tomokaku, kinou wa kono keitai denwa ga ichiban desu.
examples.en: Design aside, this cell phone is the best in terms of functionality.

cloze.after: 、機能はこの携帯電話が一番です。

examples.literalEn: As for design, the functionality of this phone is the best.
examples.naturalEn: Design aside, this cell phone is the best in terms of functionality.

examples.jp: 彼の容姿はともかく、性格は素晴らしいです。
examples.ja: 彼の容姿はともかく、性格は素晴らしいです。
examples.romaji: Kare no youshi wa tomokaku, seikaku wa subarashii desu.
examples.en: His appearance aside, he has a wonderful personality.
examples.literalEn: Putting aside his looks, his personality is wonderful.
examples.naturalEn: His appearance aside, he has a wonderful personality.

examples.jp: 料理の味はともかく、盛り付けは綺麗です。
examples.ja: 料理の味はともかく、盛り付けは綺麗です。
examples.romaji: Ryouri no aji wa tomokaku, moritsuke wa kirei desu.
examples.en: Regardless of how the food tastes, the presentation is beautiful.
examples.literalEn: Putting aside the taste of the food, the presentation is beautiful.
examples.naturalEn: Regardless of how the food tastes, the presentation is beautiful.

examples.jp: 値段はともかく、このバッグの質は良いです。
examples.ja: 値段はともかく、このバッグの質は良いです。
examples.romaji: Nedan wa tomokaku, kono baggu no shitsu wa yoi desu.
examples.en: Putting the price aside, this bag is of good quality.

cloze.after: 、このバッグの質は良いです。

examples.literalEn: Ignoring the price, this bag’s quality is good.
examples.naturalEn: Putting the price aside, this bag is of good quality.

notes.nuance: The expression “～はともかく～は” means “Used to compare or contrast two elements; ‘as for...’.” It is an important grammar point at the JLPT N2 level and is widely used in objective explanations and everyday conversation.
notes.contrast: When compared to other particles and conjunctive forms used in context, “～はともかく～は” has the characteristic of clearly indicating the speaker’s intent and focus.
notes.pitfalls: Please be careful of conjugation errors in the "Noun1 is one thing, but Noun2 is..." construction. It is important to use the dictionary form, the "te" form, and the correct particles accurately.

points.title: ～はまだしも (〜wa mada shimo)
points.meaning: Expresses that while the first item is somewhat acceptable, the second item is not.
points.explanation: The ～はまだしも grammar point is used to show a contrast where the first item or situation might still be understandable or tolerable, whereas the second one is harder to accept. It’s often translated as 'X is one thing, but Y...'.
points.short: Expresses that while the first item is somewhat acceptable, the second item is not.
points.long: The ～はまだしも grammar point is used to show a contrast where the first item or situation might still be understandable or tolerable, whereas the second one is harder to accept. It’s often translated as 'X is one thing, but Y...'.
formation: Noun1 + はまだしも + Noun2

examples.jp: 失敗するのはまだしも、やらないで後悔する方がつらい。
examples.ja: 失敗するのはまだしも、やらないで後悔する方がつらい。
examples.romaji: Shippai suru no wa mada shimo, yaranai de koukai suru hou ga tsurai.
examples.en: Failing is one thing, but regretting not having tried is even harder to bear.

cloze.after: 、やらないで後悔する方がつらい。

examples.literalEn: Failing is one thing, but regretting not even trying is worse.
examples.naturalEn: Failing is one thing, but regretting not having tried is even harder to bear.

examples.jp: このピザは野菜が少ないのはまだしも、味も悪い。
examples.ja: このピザは野菜が少ないのはまだしも、味も悪い。
examples.romaji: Kono piza wa yasai ga sukunai no wa mada shimo, aji mo warui.
examples.en: Not only does this pizza have few vegetables, but it also tastes bad.

cloze.before: このピザは野菜が少ないの

examples.literalEn: It’s not just that this pizza has few vegetables, it also tastes bad.
examples.naturalEn: Not only does this pizza have few vegetables, but it also tastes bad.

examples.jp: たまに遅刻するのはまだしも、連絡もせずに遅刻するのは許せない。
examples.ja: たまに遅刻するのはまだしも、連絡もせずに遅刻するのは許せない。
examples.romaji: Tama ni chikoku suru no wa mada shimo, renraku mo sezu ni chikoku suru no wa yurusenai.
examples.en: It’s one thing to be late occasionally, but being late without even letting anyone know is unacceptable.

cloze.after: 、連絡もせずに遅刻するのは許せない。

examples.literalEn: Being late occasionally might be forgivable, but being late without any contact is unacceptable.
examples.naturalEn: It’s one thing to be late occasionally, but being late without even letting anyone know is unacceptable.

examples.jp: 難しい質問に答えられないのはまだしも、簡単な質問にも答えられないのは問題だ。
examples.ja: 難しい質問に答えられないのはまだしも、簡単な質問にも答えられないのは問題だ。
examples.romaji: Muzukashii shitsumon ni kotaerarenai no wa mada shimo, kantan na shitsumon ni mo kotaerarenai no wa mondai da.
examples.en: It’s one thing not to be able to answer difficult questions, but it’s a problem if you can’t even answer simple ones.

cloze.before: 難しい質問に答えられないの
cloze.after: 、簡単な質問にも答えられないのは問題だ。

examples.literalEn: It’s one thing not to be able to answer difficult questions, but it’s a real problem if you can’t even answer simple ones.
examples.naturalEn: It’s one thing not to be able to answer difficult questions, but it’s a problem if you can’t even answer simple ones.

notes.nuance: The expression “～はまだしも” means “Expresses that while the first item is somewhat acceptable, the second item is not.” It is an important grammar point at the JLPT N2 level and is widely used in objective explanations and everyday conversation.
notes.contrast: When compared to other particles and conjunctive forms used in context, “～はまだしも” has the characteristic of clearly indicating the speaker’s intent and focus.
notes.pitfalls: Please be careful of mistakes in conjugation with the “-hamashimo” construction (Noun1 + はまだしも + Noun2). It is important to use the dictionary form and “te” form correctly and choose the appropriate particles.

points.title: ～はもとより (〜wa moto yori)
points.meaning: Expressing that something is obvious, and there is also something else.
points.explanation: The ～はもとより grammar point is used to emphasize that something is obvious or a given, and on top of that, there’s another aspect to consider. It translates to 'not only…but also…' or 'of course…and also…'.
points.short: Expressing that something is obvious, and there is also something else.
points.long: The ～はもとより grammar point is used to emphasize that something is obvious or a given, and on top of that, there’s another aspect to consider. It translates to 'not only…but also…' or 'of course…and also…'.
formation: Noun1 + はもとより, Noun2 + も

examples.jp: 英語はもとより、スペイン語も勉強しています。
examples.ja: 英語はもとより、スペイン語も勉強しています。
examples.romaji: Eigo wa moto yori, supeingo mo benkyou shite imasu.

examples.literalEn: I'm studying not only English, but also Spanish.
examples.naturalEn: I’m studying not only English but also Spanish.

examples.jp: 彼女は料理はもとより、お菓子作りも得意です。

examples.literalEn: This hotel not only has clean rooms but also great service.
examples.naturalEn: Not only are the rooms clean at this hotel, but the service is also excellent.

examples.jp: 彼は音楽はもとより、絵も上手です。
examples.ja: 彼は音楽はもとより、絵も上手です。
examples.romaji: Kare wa ongaku wa moto yori, e mo jouzu desu.
examples.en: He is good at painting, not to mention music.
examples.literalEn: He’s not only good at music, but also skilled at drawing.
examples.naturalEn: He is good at painting, not to mention music.

notes.nuance: The expression “～はもとより” is used to “express that something is obvious, and that there is also something else.” It is an important grammar point at the JLPT N2 level and is widely used in objective explanations and everyday conversation.
notes.contrast: When compared to other particles and conjunctive forms used in context, “～はもとより” has the characteristic of clearly indicating the speaker’s intent and focus.
notes.pitfalls: Please be careful of mistakes in conjugation when using the “not only…but also” construction (Noun1 + hamoto yori, Noun2 + mo). It is important to use the dictionary form and the “te” form correctly and to choose the appropriate particles.

points.title: ～は抜きにして (〜wa nuki ni shite)
points.meaning: Leaving aside, excluding.
points.explanation: The ～は抜きにして grammar point is used to express the idea of 'leaving aside' or 'excluding' a certain aspect. It is often used to focus the discussion or judgment on something else by disregarding the omitted point.
points.short: Leaving aside, excluding.
points.long: The ～は抜きにして grammar point is used to express the idea of 'leaving aside' or 'excluding' a certain aspect. It is often used to focus the discussion or judgment on something else by disregarding the omitted point.
formation: Noun + は抜きにして

examples.naturalEn: Setting the design aside, this cell phone has excellent features.

examples.jp: 運転の速さは抜きにして、彼女は親切で信頼できる運転手だ。
examples.ja: 運転の速さは抜きにして、彼女は親切で信頼できる運転手だ。
examples.romaji: Unten no hayasa wa nuki ni shite, kanojo wa shinsetsu de shinrai dekiru untenshu da.
examples.en: Setting aside how fast she drives, she is a kind and reliable driver.

cloze.after: 、彼女は親切で信頼できる運転手だ。

examples.literalEn: Leaving aside her driving speed, she's a kind and trustworthy driver.
examples.naturalEn: Setting aside how fast she drives, she is a kind and reliable driver.

notes.nuance: The expression “～は抜きにして” means “leaving aside” or “excluding.” It is an important grammar point at the JLPT N2 level and is widely used in objective explanations and everyday conversation.
notes.contrast: When compared to other particles and conjunctive forms used in context, “～は抜きにして” has the characteristic of clearly indicating the speaker’s intent or focus.
notes.pitfalls: Please be careful of conjugation errors in the "tsunage" form (without the "ha"). It is important to use the dictionary form, the "te" form, and the correct particles accurately.

points.title: ～べきではない (〜beki dewa nai)
points.meaning: Express that an action should not be done; 'should not', 'ought not to'.
points.explanation: The ～べきではない grammar point is used to indicate that an action is not recommended or should not be done. It can be translated as 'should not' or 'ought not to' in English. The typical formation is “Verb-dictionary form + べきではない.”
points.short: Express that an action should not be done; 'should not', 'ought not to'.
points.long: The ～べきではない grammar point is used to indicate that an action is not recommended or should not be done. It can be translated as 'should not' or 'ought not to' in English. The typical formation is “Verb-dictionary form + べきではない.”

examples.naturalEn: You shouldn’t speak ill of children.

points.title: ～まい (〜mai)
points.meaning: Express a negative conjecture or determination; 'probably not' or 'I will not'.
points.explanation: The ～まい grammar point is used to express a negative conjecture or a strong determination not to do something. In modern usage, it is generally used with the dictionary form of verbs (来る→来るまい, する→するまい, etc.). It can be translated as 'probably not' or 'I will not' in English.
points.short: Express a negative conjecture or determination; 'probably not' or 'I will not'.
points.long: The ～まい grammar point is used to express a negative conjecture or a strong determination not to do something. In modern usage, it is generally used with the dictionary form of verbs (来る→来るまい, する→するまい, etc.). It can be translated as 'probably not' or 'I will not' in English.

points.title: ～まで～て (〜made 〜te)
points.meaning: Express doing something until a certain time or condition; 'until', 'to'.

points.short: Express doing something until a certain time or condition; 'until', 'to'.

points.title: ～ままに (〜mama ni)
points.meaning: Act according to; leave as is; unchanged.
points.explanation: The ～ままに grammar point is used to express leaving something in its current state or doing something exactly as is. It can also imply doing something naturally or without altering the circumstances. Depending on the part of speech, different particles are used: Verb-て + まま, い-Adjective + のまま, な-Adjective + なまま, Noun + のまま.
points.short: Act according to; leave as is; unchanged.
points.long: The ～ままに grammar point is used to express leaving something in its current state or doing something exactly as is. It can also imply doing something naturally or without altering the circumstances. Depending on the part of speech, different particles are used: Verb-て + まま, い-Adjective + のまま, な-Adjective + なまま, Noun + のまま.

points.title: ～もかまわず (〜mo kamawazu)
points.meaning: Express indifference or disregard; 'without hesitating', 'without worrying about'.
points.explanation: The ～もかまわず grammar point is used to express indifference or disregard toward possible consequences or external factors. It can be translated as 'without hesitating', 'without worrying about', or 'regardless of'. It attaches to verbs in their dictionary form or nouns.
points.short: Express indifference or disregard; 'without hesitating', 'without worrying about'.
points.long: The ～もかまわず grammar point is used to express indifference or disregard toward possible consequences or external factors. It can be translated as 'without hesitating', 'without worrying about', or 'regardless of'. It attaches to verbs in their dictionary form or nouns.

points.title: ～ものか (〜mono ka)
points.meaning: Definitely not; no way; no chance.
points.explanation: The ～ものか grammar point is used to express a strong denial, refusal, or astonishment. It often appears with a rhetorical question tone in casual forms, such as Verb (dictionary/volitional/～たい) + ものか, Adjective + ものか, or Noun + ものか, meaning 'No way...', 'As if I'd ever...', etc.
points.short: Definitely not; no way; no chance.
points.long: The ～ものか grammar point is used to express a strong denial, refusal, or astonishment. It often appears with a rhetorical question tone in casual forms, such as Verb (dictionary/volitional/～たい) + ものか, Adjective + ものか, or Noun + ものか, meaning 'No way...', 'As if I'd ever...', etc.

points.title: ～ものがある (〜mono ga aru)

It is often used with verbs (plain form), い-adjectives, or な-adjectives + な, to show that one ‘feels strongly that...’ or ‘there’s something about it that…’.
points.short: Express a strong impression or feeling; 'there's something about it that...'

points.title: ～ものだ (〜mono da)

points.short: Expresses something natural or expected; 'it is normal that...', 'should', 'ought to'.
points.long: 「～ものだ」 can indicate that something is regarded as a general truth, common sense, or natural behavior. It can also express strong sentiment or emotion. In the past tense (Verb-た form + ものだ), it often shows nostalgia or recollection ('I used to...').

points.title: ～ものだから (〜mono dakara)
points.meaning: Express the reason or cause for something; 'because', 'since', 'due to'.
points.explanation: 「～ものだから」 is used to explain a reason or cause from the speaker’s point of view. It can be translated as 'because', 'since', or 'due to'. It often carries the nuance of 'you see, that's why ...'.
points.short: Express the reason or cause for something; 'because', 'since', 'due to'.
points.long: 「～ものだから」 is used to explain a reason or cause from the speaker’s point of view. It can be translated as 'because', 'since', or 'due to'. It often carries the nuance of 'you see, that's why ...'.

points.title: ～ものではない (〜mono dewa nai)
points.meaning: Expresses a strong negative suggestion or prohibition: 'should not', 'must not'.
points.explanation: 「～ものではない」 is used to indicate that something should not or must not be done. It often appears in written or formal contexts, meaning 'it is not proper to...' or 'you shouldn’t...'.
points.short: Expresses a strong negative suggestion or prohibition: 'should not', 'must not'.
points.long: 「～ものではない」 is used to indicate that something should not or must not be done. It often appears in written or formal contexts, meaning 'it is not proper to...' or 'you shouldn’t...'.

points.title: ～ものなら (〜mono nara)
points.meaning: Expresses a conditional wish or unlikely possibility; 'if only', 'if it were possible'.
points.explanation: 「～ものなら」 is used when expressing a strong wish under a hypothetical or difficult condition. It often implies that fulfilling this condition is unlikely or very hard, but 'if only it could happen, then...'.
points.short: Expresses a conditional wish or unlikely possibility; 'if only', 'if it were possible'.
points.long: 「～ものなら」 is used when expressing a strong wish under a hypothetical or difficult condition. It often implies that fulfilling this condition is unlikely or very hard, but 'if only it could happen, then...'.

points.title: ～ものの、～ (〜mono no、～)
points.meaning: Indicates contrast or contradiction between two clauses; 'although', 'but'.
points.explanation: 「～ものの」 is used to connect two parts of a sentence where the first part is true, yet the second part shows a contrasting or unexpected outcome. It can be translated as 'although', 'even though', or 'but still'.
points.short: Indicates contrast or contradiction between two clauses; 'although', 'but'.
points.long: 「～ものの」 is used to connect two parts of a sentence where the first part is true, yet the second part shows a contrasting or unexpected outcome. It can be translated as 'although', 'even though', or 'but still'.

points.title: ～も～ば～も～ (〜mo〜ba〜mo〜)
points.meaning: Lists multiple attributes or actions applying to the same subject: 'both…and…', 'not only…but also…'.
points.explanation: 「～も～ば～も～」 is used when describing multiple characteristics or actions. It often appears with the conditional form (ば) plus も, indicating that 'A is true, and also B is true.' For example, 'He can do X, and he can also do Y.' It's different from '～ば～ほど', which means 'the more… the more…'.
points.short: Lists multiple attributes or actions applying to the same subject: 'both…and…', 'not only…but also…'.
points.long: 「～も～ば～も～」 is used when describing multiple characteristics or actions. It often appears with the conditional form (ば) plus も, indicating that 'A is true, and also B is true.' points.explanation: 「～も同然だ」 means something is practically the same as (X). It emphasizes that although it may not be literally identical, there is hardly any difference in reality.

points.explanation: 「～を中心に」 is used with nouns to show that an action or situation is mainly or primarily about the specified noun. It can be translated as 'centered on', 'focusing on', or 'with ... as the main focus'.

points.title: ～上で (〜ue de)
points.meaning: Used to express that something is done after or on the basis of something else; 'after', 'upon'.
points.explanation: The ～上で grammar point is used to indicate that an action or decision is made after another action or condition, or based on certain information. It can be translated as 'after doing something' or 'on the basis of...'.
points.short: Used to express that something is done after or on the basis of something else; 'after', 'upon'.
points.long: The ～上で grammar point is used to indicate that an action or decision is made after another action or condition, or based on certain information. It can be translated as 'after doing something' or 'on the basis of...'.

points.title: ～上に (〜ue ni)
points.meaning: Express 'in addition to', 'besides', 'not only... but also'.
points.explanation: The ～上に grammar point is used to indicate that there is an additional piece of information or situation besides the first one. It can be translated as 'in addition to', 'besides', or 'not only... but also'. It can be used with verbs, い-adjectives, な-adjectives, and nouns.
points.short: Express 'in addition to', 'besides', 'not only... but also'.
points.long: The ～上に grammar point is used to indicate that there is an additional piece of information or situation besides the first one. It can be translated as 'in addition to', 'besides', or 'not only... but also'. It can be used with verbs, い-adjectives, な-adjectives, and nouns.

points.title: ～上は (～ue wa)
points.meaning: Expresses 'now that', 'since', or 'once'.
points.explanation: The ～上は grammar point is used to express that since a certain condition or situation exists, a certain action or result follows. It can be translated as 'now that', 'since', or 'once' in English. The formation differs depending on whether it is used with a verb, い-adjective, な-adjective, or noun.
points.short: Expresses 'now that', 'since', or 'once'.
points.long: The ～上は grammar point is used to express that since a certain condition or situation exists, a certain action or result follows. points.title: ～恐れがある (〜osore ga aru)
points.meaning: Express a concern or fear that something undesirable might occur.
points.explanation: The ～恐れがある grammar point indicates that there is a concern or fear that something undesirable or negative might happen. It is often used for potential problems or risks, and can be translated as 'there is a risk' or 'there is a possibility'.
points.short: Express a concern or fear that something undesirable might occur.
points.long: The ～恐れがある grammar point indicates that there is a concern or fear that something undesirable or negative might happen. It is often used for potential problems or risks, and can be translated as 'there is a risk' or 'there is a possibility'.

points.title: ～折には (〜ori ni wa)

points.explanation: The ～折には grammar point is used to emphasize a specific moment or situation (often not very frequent). It can be translated as 'when (the occasion arises)' or 'in case of'.
points.short: Expresses 'when' or 'in case of' specific situations or timings.
points.long: The ～折には grammar point is used to emphasize a specific moment or situation (often not very frequent). It can be translated as 'when (the occasion arises)' or 'in case of'.

points.title: ～末 (～sue)
points.meaning: Express the outcome after a period of time or series of actions; 'after', 'as a result of'.
points.explanation: The ～末 grammar point is used to indicate an outcome or result after a period of time, effort, or a series of actions. It can be translated as 'after', 'as a result of', or 'following'. It is typically used with nouns (e.g., '相談の末', '努力の末').
points.short: Express the outcome after a period of time or series of actions; 'after', 'as a result of'.
points.long: The ～末 grammar point is used to indicate an outcome or result after a period of time, effort, or a series of actions. It can be translated as 'after', 'as a result of', or 'following'. It is typically used with nouns (e.g., '相談の末', '努力の末').

points.title: ～次第 (〜shidai)
points.meaning: Expresses 'as soon as' (when used with Verb-ますstem) or 'depending on' (when used with a noun).
points.explanation: The grammar pattern ～次第 can mean 'as soon as' when used with a verb in its ます-stem, and 'depending on' when used with a noun. For instance, 仕事が終わり次第 (as soon as work finishes) or 天気次第 (depending on the weather).
points.short: Expresses 'as soon as' (when used with Verb-ますstem) or 'depending on' (when used with a noun).
points.long: The grammar pattern ～次第 can mean 'as soon as' when used with a verb in its ます-stem, and 'depending on' when used with a noun. For instance, 仕事が終わり次第 (as soon as work finishes) or 天気次第 (depending on the weather).

points.short: Indicates 'depending on; based on' a certain factor or situation.

points.title: ～次第です (〜shidai desu)
points.meaning: A polite/formal way to say 'it depends on...' or 'as soon as...', often used in concluding statements.
points.explanation: 「～次第です」 is frequently used in more formal contexts, either to mean that something depends on certain conditions or to indicate an action will happen as soon as something else is completed. It’s also used as a set phrase to conclude an explanation in writing.
points.short: A polite/formal way to say 'it depends on...' or 'as soon as...', often used in concluding statements.
points.long: 「～次第です」 is frequently used in more formal contexts, either to mean that something depends on certain conditions or to indicate an action will happen as soon as something else is completed. It’s also used as a set phrase to conclude an explanation in writing.

examples.literalEn: It depends on my exam results, but I'm considering studying abroad.

examples.jp: お客様のご意見次第で新メニューを追加する次第です。
examples.ja: お客様のご意見次第で新メニューを追加する次第です。
examples.romaji: Okyakusama no goiken shidai de shin menyuu wo tsuika suru shidai desu.
examples.en: We will add new menu items based on customer feedback.

cloze.before: お客様のご意見次第で新メニューを追加する

examples.literalEn: We intend to add a new menu item depending on our customers’ feedback.
examples.naturalEn: We will add new menu items based on customer feedback.

examples.jp: 申請が完了次第ですので、手続きが終わったらパスポートを受け取れます。
examples.ja: 申請が完了次第ですので、手続きが終わったらパスポートを受け取れます。
examples.romaji: Shinsei ga kanryou shidai desu no de, tetsudzuki ga owattara pasupooto wo uketoremasu.
examples.en: Since the application is complete, you will be able to pick up your passport once the process is finished.

cloze.after: ので、手続きが終わったらパスポートを受け取れます。

examples.literalEn: As soon as the application is completed, you'll be able to receive your passport.
examples.naturalEn: Since the application is complete, you will be able to pick up your passport once the process is finished.

notes.nuance: The expression “～次第です” means “A polite/formal way to say ‘it depends on...’ or ‘as soon as...’, often used in concluding statements.” It is an important grammar point at the JLPT N2 level and is widely used in objective explanations and everyday conversation.
notes.contrast: When compared to other particles and conjunctive forms used in context, “～次第です” is characterized by its ability to clearly indicate the speaker’s intent and focus.
notes.pitfalls: Please be careful of conjugation errors in the "-shite" construction (Verb-masu stem + shite desu (or Noun + shite desu)). It is important to use the dictionary form and the "te" form correctly and to choose the appropriate particles.

points.title: ～気味 (〜gimi)
points.meaning: Indicates a slight feeling or tendency toward a particular state.
points.explanation: The suffix ～気味 generally attaches to nouns (or nominalized words) to express a slight feeling, tendency, or inclination toward a particular state. It often translates to '-ish' or 'a bit' in English (e.g., 'sleep-deprived-ish', 'nervous-ish').
points.short: Indicates a slight feeling or tendency toward a particular state.
points.long: The suffix ～気味 generally attaches to nouns (or nominalized words) to express a slight feeling, tendency, or inclination toward a particular state. It often translates to '-ish' or 'a bit' in English (e.g., 'sleep-deprived-ish', 'nervous-ish').
formation: Noun + 気味 (e.g., 風邪気味, 寝不足気味, 緊張気味)

examples.jp: 最近寝不足気味で、ちょっと疲れています。
examples.ja: 最近寝不足気味で、ちょっと疲れています。
examples.romaji: Saikin nebusoku gimi de, chotto tsukarete imasu.
examples.en: I haven't been getting enough sleep lately, so I'm feeling a little tired.

cloze.after: で、ちょっと疲れています。

examples.literalEn: Lately, I'm feeling somewhat sleep-deprived and a bit tired.
examples.naturalEn: I haven't been getting enough sleep lately, so I'm feeling a little tired.

examples.jp: この部屋は暗い気味だから、もっと明るい照明をつけよう。
examples.ja: この部屋は暗い気味だから、もっと明るい照明をつけよう。
examples.romaji: Kono heya wa kurai gimi dakara, motto akarui shoumei wo tsukeyou.
examples.en: This room is a bit dark, so let’s turn on a brighter light.

cloze.after: だから、もっと明るい照明をつけよう。

examples.literalEn: This room is a bit dark, so let's install brighter lighting.
examples.naturalEn: This room is a bit dark, so let’s turn on a brighter light.

examples.jp: 彼女は緊張気味で話していました。
examples.ja: 彼女は緊張気味で話していました。
examples.romaji: Kanojo wa kinchou gimi de hanashite imashita.
examples.en: She was speaking somewhat nervously.
examples.literalEn: She was speaking somewhat nervously.
examples.naturalEn: She was speaking somewhat nervously.

examples.jp: 彼の声は風邪気味だったね。
examples.ja: 彼の声は風邪気味だったね。
examples.romaji: Kare no koe wa kaze gimi datta ne.
examples.en: His voice sounded a bit hoarse.
examples.literalEn: His voice sounded like he might have a slight cold.
examples.naturalEn: His voice sounded a bit hoarse.

notes.nuance: The expression “～気味” indicates “a slight feeling or tendency toward a particular state.” It is an important grammatical point at the JLPT N2 level and is widely used in objective descriptions and everyday conversation.
notes.contrast: When compared to other particles and conjunctive forms used in context, “～気味” has the characteristic of clearly indicating the speaker’s intent and focus.
notes.pitfalls: Please be careful of conjugation errors in constructions involving “-gimi” (e.g., “kaze-gimi,” “nesufuku-gimi,” “tenshō-gimi”). It is important to use the dictionary form and “te” form correctly and to choose the appropriate particles.

points.title: ～限り (〜kagiri)
points.meaning: Expresses 'as long as', 'while', or 'to the extent that' a certain condition holds true.
points.explanation: The phrase ～限り is used to indicate that something continues or is true 'as long as' or 'while' a certain condition is met. It can also mean 'to the extent that'.
points.short: Expresses 'as long as', 'while', or 'to the extent that' a certain condition holds true.
points.long: The phrase ～限り is used to indicate that something continues or is true 'as long as' or 'while' a certain condition is met. It can also mean 'to the extent that'.
formation: Verb-casual + 限り, い-Adjective + 限り, な-Adjective + な限り, Noun + の限り

examples.jp: 元気な限り、運動し続けます。
examples.ja: 元気な限り、運動し続けます。
examples.romaji: Genki na kagiri, undou shi tsuzukemasu.
examples.en: As long as I have the energy, I’ll keep exercising.
examples.literalEn: As long as I'm healthy, I'll keep exercising.
examples.naturalEn: As long as I have the energy, I’ll keep exercising.

examples.jp: お金がある限り、旅行を楽しみたい。
examples.ja: お金がある限り、旅行を楽しみたい。
examples.romaji: Okane ga aru kagiri, ryokou o tanoshimitai.
examples.en: As long as I have money, I want to enjoy traveling.
examples.literalEn: As long as I have money, I'd like to travel.
examples.naturalEn: As long as I have money, I want to enjoy traveling.

examples.jp: 彼が話し続ける限り、このプロジェクトのメリットが伝わるでしょう。
examples.ja: 彼が話し続ける限り、このプロジェクトのメリットが伝わるでしょう。
examples.romaji: Kare ga hanashi tsudzukeru kagiri, kono purojekuto no meritto ga tsutawaru deshou.
examples.en: As long as he keeps talking, the benefits of this project will come across.

cloze.after: 、このプロジェクトのメリットが伝わるでしょう。

examples.literalEn: As long as he keeps talking about it, the benefits of this project will be conveyed.
examples.naturalEn: As long as he keeps talking, the benefits of this project will come across.

examples.jp: 勉強する限り、試験に合格できる可能性が高まります。
examples.ja: 勉強する限り、試験に合格できる可能性が高まります。
examples.romaji: Benkyou suru kagiri, shiken ni goukaku dekiru kanousei ga takamarimasu.
examples.en: The more you study, the higher your chances of passing the exam.

cloze.after: 、試験に合格できる可能性が高まります。

examples.literalEn: As long as you study, you'll have a higher chance of passing the exam.
examples.naturalEn: The more you study, the higher your chances of passing the exam.

notes.nuance: The expression “～限り” means “as long as,” “while,” or “to the extent that” a certain condition holds true. It is an important grammar point at the JLPT N2 level and is widely used in objective explanations and everyday conversation.
notes.contrast: Compared to other particles and conjunctive forms used in context, “～限り” has the characteristic of clearly indicating the speaker’s intent and focus.
notes.pitfalls: Please be careful of conjugation errors in the “-kiri” construction (Verb-casual + -kiri, i-adjective + -kiri, na-adjective + -na-kiri, noun + -no-kiri). It is important to use the dictionary form and “te” form correctly and to choose the appropriate particles.

points.title: ～際に (〜sai ni)
points.meaning: Means 'when', 'while', or 'on the occasion of' a certain event or situation.
points.explanation: ～際に is used to specify a time or occasion when something happens. It’s more formal than a simple 'とき' and often appears in announcements or polite instructions.
points.short: Means 'when', 'while', or 'on the occasion of' a certain event or situation.
points.long: ～際に is used to specify a time or occasion when something happens. It’s more formal than a simple 'とき' and often appears in announcements or polite instructions.
formation: Verb-casual + 際に, い-Adjective + 際に, な-Adjective + な際に, Noun + の際に

examples.jp: 出発の際に、パスポートを忘れないでください。
examples.ja: 出発の際に、パスポートを忘れないでください。
examples.romaji: Shuppatsu no sai ni, pasupooto wo wasurenai de kudasai.
examples.en: Please don’t forget your passport when you leave.

cloze.after: 、パスポートを忘れないでください。

examples.literalEn: When departing, please don't forget your passport.
examples.naturalEn: Please don’t forget your passport when you leave.

examples.jp: 地震が起こる際に、すぐに避難してください。
examples.ja: 地震が起こる際に、すぐに避難してください。
examples.romaji: Jishin ga okoru sai ni, sugu ni hinan shite kudasai.
examples.en: If an earthquake occurs, please evacuate immediately.
examples.literalEn: When an earthquake occurs, please evacuate immediately.
examples.naturalEn: If an earthquake occurs, please evacuate immediately.

examples.jp: 日本へ来る際に、お土産をたくさん買うつもりです。
examples.ja: 日本へ来る際に、お土産をたくさん買うつもりです。
examples.romaji: Nihon e kuru sai ni, omiyage wo takusan kau tsumori desu.
examples.en: I plan to buy lots of souvenirs when I visit Japan.

cloze.after: 、お土産をたくさん買うつもりです。

examples.literalEn: When I come to Japan, I plan to buy lots of souvenirs.
examples.naturalEn: I plan to buy lots of souvenirs when I visit Japan.

examples.jp: 面接の際に、スーツを着用してください。
examples.ja: 面接の際に、スーツを着用してください。
examples.romaji: Mensetsu no sai ni, suutsu wo chakuyou shite kudasai.
examples.en: Please wear a suit to the interview.

cloze.after: 、スーツを着用してください。

examples.literalEn: Please wear a suit when attending the interview.
examples.naturalEn: Please wear a suit to the interview.

notes.nuance: The expression “～際に” means “when,” “while,” or “on the occasion of” a certain event or situation. It is an important grammar point at the JLPT N2 level and is widely used in objective explanations and everyday conversation.
notes.contrast: When compared to other particles and conjunctive forms used in context, “～際に” is characterized by its ability to clearly indicate the speaker’s intent or focus.
notes.pitfalls: Please be careful of conjugation errors in the “tsunage” form (Verb-casual + “ni,” i-adjective + “ni,” na-adjective + “na ni,” noun + “no ni”). It is important to use the dictionary form and “te” form correctly and to choose the appropriate particles.
